description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_user_profile
entries.description:
Retrieve profile information for a specific Jira user.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    user_identifier: User identifier (email, username, key, or account ID).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira user profile object, or an error object if not found.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

user_identifier.description: Identifier for the user (e.g., email address 'user@example.com', username 'johndoe', account ID 'accountid:...', or key for Server/DC).

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

(6) pure FE / shared FE+BE / needs architecture input? (7) sizeable now or needs clarification?
B. The four standing axes with anything ambiguous flagged: behaviour, desktop/mobile, a11y, data.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_batch_get_changelogs
entries.description:
Get changelogs for multiple Jira issues (Cloud only).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_ids_or_keys: List of issue IDs or keys.
    fields: List of fields to filter changelogs by. None for all fields.
    limit: Maximum changelogs per issue (-1 for all).

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of issues with their changelogs.

Raises:
    NotImplementedError: If run on Jira Server/Data Center.
    ValueError: If Jira client is unavailable.

issue_ids_or_keys.description: Comma-separated list of Jira issue IDs or keys (e.g. 'PROJ-123,PROJ-124')

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to filter changelogs by (e.g. 'status,assignee'). Default to None for all fields.

limit.description: Maximum number of changelogs to return in result for each issue. Default to -1 for all changelogs. Notice that it only limits the results in the response, the function will still fetch all the data.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_agile_boards
entries.description:
Get jira agile boards by name, project key, or type.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    board_name: Name of the board (fuzzy search).
    project_key: Project key.
    board_type: Board type ('scrum' or 'kanban').
    start_at: Starting index.
    limit: Maximum results.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of board objects.

board_name.description: (Optional) The name of board, support fuzzy search

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_sprints_from_board
entries.description:
Get jira sprints from board by state.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    board_id: The ID of the board.
    state: Sprint state ('active', 'future', 'closed'). If None, returns all sprints.
    start_at: Starting index.
    limit: Maximum results.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of sprint objects.

    "content": {
      "value": "Jira Story Workflow for SFCC Project
====================================

This page explains the expected Jira workflow for user stories in the SFCC project, including what each status means and the actions expected from the team while a story is in that state.

Proposed Change: To Do -> In BA -> Ready for Review (PO sign off) -> In Tech Design (once solution is clear, conversation with developers/QA, address open points) -> Ready for Dev

Handovers: BA → SA

| **Stage in board** | **Jira Workflow Status** | **Assignee** | **Expected actions during this state** | **Automations** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Backlog | **To Do** | BA | Capture the story request, business need, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and any supporting links or assets. Business Analyst begins drafting the story for review. |  |
| Refinement | **In Refinement** | BA | Business Analyst writes and refines the story - including acceptance criteria, designs, business rules, dependencies and any supporting links or assets. Story is not ready for technical review until BA work is complete. |  |
| Refinement | **Ready for Review** | BA - PO - BA | Story is complete from a business and requirements perspective. Product Owner reviews and signs off before the story is passed to technical design. |  |
| Refinement | **In Tech Design** | BA - SA | Define and document the technical solution. Confirm impacted SFCC cartridges, services, jobs, integrations, data model changes, configuration updates, API contracts, security and performance considerations, and deployment approach. Developers and QA are involved at this stage to address open points and confirm the approach. Story is sized and estimated here. Capture design decisions, dependencies, risks, and any required technical tasks in Jira. The Definition of Ready Checklist must be completed and up to date before a story can be moved to Ready for Development. | The Definition of Ready Checklist must be completed and up to date before a Story can be moved to Ready for Development \* [Automation Rule](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/SFCC/settings/automation#/rule/019eb9c3-9d77-7d1b-bc07-5737c112576d) |
| Blocked | **Blocked** | The person working on the story | The team raises it immediately in standup, assigns an owner, and add details on the User Story before the transition completes. The SM logs it in the RAID log, follows up daily, and escalates to the Delivery Lead if there is no response within 24 hours. Meanwhile, the developer picks up a stretch story. The SM verifies resolution before applying the Unblock transition. |  |
| Ready for Development | **Ready for Development** | SM | Confirm the story is assigned, sprint committed, and unblocked. Developers validate branch strategy, environment access, SFCC instance availability, API credentials, test data, and any required design or configuration inputs. | Ticket is moved to In Progress if commits are raised for a ticket  \* [Automation rule](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/SFCC/settings/automation#/rule/019eba1f-0258-7369-a471-ff1c40cb8660) |
| Development | **In Progress** | Developer | Implement the change in SFCC, including code, configuration, templates, controllers, jobs, services, or Business Manager updates as required. Keep the Jira story updated, raise blockers early, and link commits or pull requests. |  |
| Development | **Code Review** | Dev Lead | Submit the pull request and request review from the appropriate technical reviewers. Review code quality, SFCC best practices, security, performance, test coverage, and alignment with acceptance criteria. Address review feedback before moving forward. | Once PR is Merged ticket status is updated to Ready for QA \* [Automation rule](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/SFCC/settings/automation#/rule/019eba20-3e99-7ebb-aa1c-40bf5f071972) |
| Testing | **Ready for QA** | QA | Deploy the change to the QA environment, provide test notes, impacted areas, configuration steps, and any sample data needed. Confirm the build is stable and the story is ready for QA validation. |  |
| Testing | **In QA** | QA | QA validates the story against acceptance criteria, regression impact, browser/device coverage, storefront behavior, Business Manager configuration, integrations, and edge cases. Defects are logged and linked to the story.  If passed, QA to coordinate with developer to deploy to SIT |  |
| Testing | **In SIT** | QA | Change is deployed SIT environment and QA to validate the story against acceptance criteria, regression impact, browser/device coverage, storefront behavior, Business Manager configuration, integrations, and edge cases. Defects are logged and linked to the story. |  |
| Testing | **Ready to deploy to UAT** | Developer | Developer that developed the story should deploy to UAT environment |  |
| UAT | **Ready for UAT** | PO | Confirm QA sign-off and prepare the story for business validation. Provide release notes, testing instructions, credentials if needed, and any known limitations for Product Owner or business stakeholders. |  |
| UAT | **In UAT** | PO | Business stakeholders validate the story in the UAT environment. Product Owner confirms the feature meets business expectations and acceptance criteria. Any feedback or defects are documented in Jira. |  |
| Ready for Release | **Ready for Release** | Dev Lead | Confirm UAT approval, release readiness, deployment steps, rollback plan, feature toggles, configuration changes, and release notes. Ensure the story is included in the correct release package. |  |
| Done | **Done** |  | Confirm production deployment and post-release validation. Close the story after acceptance criteria are met, documentation is updated, and any follow-up tasks or defects are created if required. | The Definition of Done Checklist must be completed and up to date before a Story can be moved to Done  \* [Automation rule](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/SFCC/settings/automation#/rule/019eb9c5-0168-7d8d-9862-193fb921066a) |

      "value": "What we need to finalise user stories per epic
----------------------------------------------

PWA Kit user stories cannot be written, reviewed or signed off until the relevant design components are locked. Here is what that means in practice.

### 1 — Components must be finalised first

* Before user stories can be written for an epic e.g. Checkout Flow & Delivery, **every UI component that appears in that epic must be finalised in the UI kit** — fully componentised in Figma with all variations, states and responsive sizes accounted for. This allows us to build the component user story.
* Each component is owned by the **earliest epic in the sequence where it appears**. That epic is responsible for designing all variations of that component — including any variations needed by later epics. For example, if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage, all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP.

> As we move through the epic sequence, design effort should reduce. By the time we reach epics like Homepage or Wishlist, most components should already exist. Design at that stage should be limited to anything genuinely net-new.

### 2 — Design freeze

* **Hard rule:** Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only. Any change after lock requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component.

### 3 — Sign-off checklist per epic

* Before component user stories are submitted for PO review, confirm the component has ALL variations included in the UI kit.

Site: `zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net` · Space: **SFCC** (display name varies between "Space SFCC" and "Adobe SFCC" in API responses — same space). **Read-only throughout; nothing was written, created, updated, or commented on.**

## TASK 2 (headline) — the 04.71 decomposition page EXISTS and I read it in full

**Page ID `400195600` — exact title: `04.71 Writing User Stories for Components`** (version 2)
`https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/400195600`

It is short — ~330 words total. Here is the **entire page verbatim**, so nothing is filtered:

> ### How to write user stories for the Zimmermann build
>
> #### Overview
>
> User stories are organised across two levels: component epics and page epics. Each serves a different purpose and audience.
>
> ---
>
> #### Level 1 — Component epics
>
> This is the build story for each individual component. It covers what the component does, its variants and configurations, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states.
>
> **There are two types of component, and this determines how many stories you write:**
>
> **PWA Kit only** (e.g. Button, Textfield, Dropdown, Cart Item)
> These are functional UI components with no content authoring required. Write one story, in the PWA Kit epic only. No Contentful story is needed.
>
> **Contentful + PWA Kit** (e.g. Banner, Editorial Cards, Footer, Navigation)
> These components have content that an editor manages. Write two stories:
>
> * One in the **Contentful epic** — covering the content model, authoring fields, configuration options and validation rules
> * One in the **PWA Kit epic** — covering how the component renders and responds to what Contentful delivers
>
> > A Contentful component always needs a PWA Kit story too, because PWA Kit has to render it. A PWA Kit-only component does not need a Contentful story.
>
> ---
>
> #### Level 2 — Page epics
>
> This is the experience story for a specific page (e.g. PDP, PLP, Checkout). Rather than focusing on individual component builds, these stories describe how components work together to deliver a user journey.
>
> Write these from the customer's perspective — for example, on the PDP: a customer selects a size using the size selector, selects a colour using the colour attribute component, and adds the item to their bag using the add to cart component.
>
> These stories should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1. They are about the interaction between components and the end-to-end experience on that page.
>
> ---
>
> #### Quick reference
>
> | Level | Epic | Focus | Written from |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | 1 | PWA Kit component | Build, variants, accessibility | Developer perspective |
> | 1 | Contentful component | Content model, authoring, field config | Merchandiser perspective |
> | 1 | PWA Kit (render) | Rendering Contentful output | Developer perspective |
> | 2 | Page (e.g. PDP) | How components work together | Shopper perspective |

### Answers to your four specific sub-questions

**(a) Level 1 vs Level 2** — quoted in full above. Level 1 = per-component build story, developer/merchandiser perspective. Level 2 = per-page experience story, shopper perspective, explicitly *not* repeating Level 1 build detail.

**(b) Component story vs page story scoping** — the only stated boundary is the one above: a component story covers "what the component does, its variants and configurations, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states"; a page story covers "how components work together to deliver a user journey" and "should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1."

**(c) Sizing / estimation of component stories — NOT ON THIS PAGE.** 04.71 contains no story points, no t-shirt sizes, no estimation guidance, no "one story per X" sizing heuristic. The word "point", "estimate", "size" and "sprint" do not appear on it at all. This is a real gap, not something I failed to find.

**(d) Component variants — a variant is part of the base component's story, not its own story.** This is stated implicitly but unambiguously, and it's the single most load-bearing line for your question:

> "This is the build story for each individual component. It covers what the component does, **its variants and configurations**, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states."

The **only** thing on this page that multiplies the story count is the PWA-Kit-only (1 story) vs Contentful+PWA-Kit (2 stories) split. Variants are explicitly named as *contents of* the one component story, and the Quick reference table reinforces it ("Focus: Build, **variants**, accessibility" sits inside the single Level 1 PWA Kit row).

### Corroborating page — sibling `04.72`, which is where the variant rule is enforced

**Page ID `408944644` — exact title: `04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker`** (version 7)

Verbatim, the load-bearing paragraphs:

> * Before user stories can be written for an epic e.g. Checkout Flow & Delivery, **every UI component that appears in that epic must be finalised in the UI kit** — fully componentised in Figma with all variations, states and responsive sizes accounted for. This allows us to build the component user story.
> * Each component is owned by the **earliest epic in the sequence where it appears**. That epic is responsible for designing all variations of that component — including any variations needed by later epics. For example, if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage, all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP.

> As we move through the epic sequence, design effort should reduce. By the time we reach epics like Homepage or Wishlist, most components should already exist. Design at that stage should be limited to anything genuinely net-new.

> **Hard rule:** Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only. Any change after lock requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component.

> Before component user stories are submitted for PO review, confirm the component has ALL variations included in the UI kit.

Note the PLP row of that tracker: **"PLP | PLP template, product grid, filter & sort panel, category header | Design components finalised: Sep 7 (Sprint 4) | User stories ready for PO review: Sep 12 | ready for development: Sep 21 | Sprint 2, Sprint 3, Sprint 4, Sprint 5 | BA lead: Jas"**. 04.72 contains **no story points or sizing** either — it is dates and ownership only.

> ### How to write user stories for the Zimmermann build
>
> #### Overview
>
> User stories are organised across two levels: component epics and page epics. Each serves a different purpose and audience.
>
> ---
>
> #### Level 1 — Component epics
>
> This is the build story for each individual component. It covers what the component does, its variants and configurations, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states.
>
> **There are two types of component, and this determines how many stories you write:**
>
> **PWA Kit only** (e.g. Button, Textfield, Dropdown, Cart Item)
> These are functional UI components with no content authoring required. Write one story, in the PWA Kit epic only. No Contentful story is needed.
>
> **Contentful + PWA Kit** (e.g. Banner, Editorial Cards, Footer, Navigation)
> These components have content that an editor manages. Write two stories:
>
> * One in the **Contentful epic** — covering the content model, authoring fields, configuration options and validation rules
> * One in the **PWA Kit epic** — covering how the component renders and responds to what Contentful delivers
>
> > A Contentful component always needs a PWA Kit story too, because PWA Kit has to render it. A PWA Kit-only component does not need a Contentful story.
>
> ---
>
> #### Level 2 — Page epics
>
> This is the experience story for a specific page (e.g. PDP, PLP, Checkout). Rather than focusing on individual component builds, these stories describe how components work together to deliver a user journey.
>
> Write these from the customer's perspective — for example, on the PDP: a customer selects a size using the size selector, selects a colour using the colour attribute component, and adds the item to their bag using the add to cart component.
>
> These stories should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1. They are about the interaction between components and the end-to-end experience on that page.
>
> ---
>
> #### Quick reference
>
> | Level | Epic | Focus | Written from |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | 1 | PWA Kit component | Build, variants, accessibility | Developer perspective |
> | 1 | Contentful component | Content model, authoring, field config | Merchandiser perspective |
> | 1 | PWA Kit (render) | Rendering Contentful output | Developer perspective |
> | 2 | Page (e.g. PDP) | How components work together | Shopper perspective |

### Answers to your four specific sub-questions

**(a) Level 1 vs Level 2** — quoted in full above. Level 1 = per-component build story, developer/merchandiser perspective. Level 2 = per-page experience story, shopper perspective, explicitly *not* repeating Level 1 build detail.

**(b) Component story vs page story scoping** — the only stated boundary is the one above: a component story covers "what the component does, its variants and configurations, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states"; a page story covers "how components work together to deliver a user journey" and "should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1."

**(c) Sizing / estimation of component stories — NOT ON THIS PAGE.** 04.71 contains no story points, no t-shirt sizes, no estimation guidance, no "one story per X" sizing heuristic. The word "point", "estimate", "size" and "sprint" do not appear on it at all. This is a real gap, not something I failed to find.

**(d) Component variants — a variant is part of the base component's story, not its own story.** This is stated implicitly but unambiguously, and it's the single most load-bearing line for your question:

> "This is the build story for each individual component. It covers what the component does, **its variants and configurations**, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states."

The **only** thing on this page that multiplies the story count is the PWA-Kit-only (1 story) vs Contentful+PWA-Kit (2 stories) split. **Page ID `408944644` — exact title: `04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker`** (version 7)

Verbatim, the load-bearing paragraphs:

> * Before user stories can be written for an epic e.g. Checkout Flow & Delivery, **every UI component that appears in that epic must be finalised in the UI kit** — fully componentised in Figma with all variations, states and responsive sizes accounted for. This allows us to build the component user story.
> * Each component is owned by the **earliest epic in the sequence where it appears**. That epic is responsible for designing all variations of that component — including any variations needed by later epics. For example, if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage, all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP.

> **Hard rule:** Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only. Any change after lock requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component.

> Before component user stories are submitted for PO review, confirm the component has ALL variations included in the UI kit.

content.content:
### dataMigrationSeo.md lines 45-80 ###
- hreflang implemented via XML sitemap format, mapping all locale codes to their respective storefront URLs (DMU-024).
- hreflang tags consolidated from the current 200+ country-specific tags to ~12 regional/language-level tags (DMU-025) — final structure to be confirmed with the Sparro SEO team prior to implementation.

### Sitemaps & robots
- XML sitemaps auto-generated per storefront and locale, refreshed daily (DMU-026). Disabled and deleted pages excluded on regeneration (DMU-027). Homepage URLs include trailing slash (DMU-028). URLs blocked in `robots.txt` must not appear in any sitemap (DMU-029).
- `robots.txt` permits crawling of indexable pages including the bag page; restricts checkout flow, account pages, search results, and filtered URL parameters (DMU-036).

### Rendering, headings & meta
- All product, category, and content pages rendered **server-side (SSR)** for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS (DMU-030).
- Title tags per page in the format `[Product Name] [Colour] | Zimmermann` — the legacy "Online" token has been removed as it consumes character space without value. Configurable via BM meta tag rules (DMU-031, updated 2026-05-15).
- Unique meta description tags per product and category page, sourced from product and catalogue data in SFCC. Category page metadata remains editable per page and is not auto-applied across all pages (DMU-032, Ready for Sign Off — Zimmermann to clarify what "auto-applied across pages" means before final sign-off).
- Single H1 per page template (homepage, PLP, PDP), correct H2–H6 hierarchy, no duplicate heading tags (DMU-033). PDP H1 includes the product colour (DMU-034).
- CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level (DMU-035, partial resolution 2026-05-15): **SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful). Still Open: Sparro to define field schema before custom build.

### Structured data
- Product and Merchant Listing Schema on all PDPs per Sparro template (DMU-037) — custom build required, not OOTB in SFCC PWA Kit.
- CollectionPage, BreadcrumbList, and ItemList Schema on all PLPs per Sparro template (DMU-038) — custom build, Accenture + Sparro to confirm JSON-LD scope and page types.
- LocalBusiness Schema on individual boutique location detail pages per Sparro template (DMU-039) — custom build.
- Organisation Schema on each regional storefront homepage per Sparro template, with `url` and `contactPoint` fields configured per storefront (DMU-040) — custom build.
- Structured data for products includes available sizes and per-offer availability, driven by real-time inventory data (DMU-041).

---

## 4. GEO (DMU-042)

The system will deliver the technical foundations required for **post-launch GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) enablement** — SSR, structured data, canonical URLs, and XML sitemaps — ensuring no architectural decisions block future GEO activation (DMU-042). No GEO-specific features are in launch scope.

---

## 5. Open Items

See **AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"** for the full list. Data migration / URL / SEO / GEO open items:

- Redirect mapping ownership and existing CDN/SEO rule audit (DMU-018, DMU-019)
- PLP canonical override on indexable filter pages (DMU-022)
- Category meta description "auto-applied across pages" — Zimmermann to clarify the concern before sign-off (DMU-032)

entries.name: mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_metadata
entries.description: IMPORTANT: Always prefer to use get_design_context tool. Get metadata for a node or page in the Figma desktop app in XML format. Useful only for getting an overview of the structure, it only includes node IDs, layer types, names, positions and sizes. You can call get_design_context on the node IDs contained in this response. Use the nodeId parameter to specify a node id, it can also be the page id (e.g. 0:1). IMPORTANT: This tool only works for Figma design files (URL path `/design/`). It is NOT supported for FigJam (`/board/`) or Slides (`/slides/`) files. This tool is not supported for Figma Make Files (URLs containing `/make/`). <result># SFCC-749 — Backlog Refinement Analysis

---

## A. Seven-point sizing lens

**(1) Front-end impact?** Yes, entirely — PWA Kit component build. Sibling SFCC-748 holds the Contentful schema half.

**(2) Requirement clear enough to size?** **No.** Three independent contradictions:

**(3) Which surfaces?** AC says breadcrumb on **every page**; SEO text on category/sub-category only. But the confirmed functional requirements only cover PDP (PRD-001) and search (SPR-46) — **PLP/category breadcrumb has no confirmed functional requirement**, only a Design Tracker row marked `PENDING` / *"26-06: Missing in design"*. "Every page" is unbounded and unpriced (cart? checkout? account?).

**(4) Design/Figma dependencies?** Design exists and is unusually complete for the SEO block — but see C, the two links disagree and the breadcrumb itself is undrawn.

**(5) API/backend dependencies?** Breadcrumb: **none, data is already there.** SEO text: blocked on SFCC-748 (no points, status Tech design) and on the Contentful-vs-SFCC decision above. If it resolves to SFCC/BM, this becomes a backend dependency that doesn't exist yet.

# SFCC-874 — Backlog Refinement Analysis

**Read-only. Nothing written to Jira, Confluence, or the codebase.**

**Headline:** SFCC-874 is **not sizeable as written**, and it is currently in `Ready for Development` in direct violation of this project's own Definition of Ready. It is **not** a variant of SFCC-743 — it is a structurally different component that happens to share the product card. It can be sized independently of SFCC-743, but not until four concrete gaps close.

---

## A. The seven-point sizing lens

**1. Front-end impact?** Yes, entirely. A net-new organism under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/`, plus a co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipe registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`. No existing file is modified except that registry.

**2. Requirement clear enough to size?** **No.** Four blockers, all evidence-backed:

- **AC 12 references props that do not exist in the ticket's own props table.** Verbatim: *"Given `size=Desktop`, when the component renders, then `imageGroup.showCarousel` controls carousel visibility and `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator` has no effect."* There is no `imageGroup` prop in the Props-in-scope table. `grep` for `showCarousel`/`showSlideIndicator` across `overrides/` returns **zero hits**. The only `imageGroup` in the codebase is SFCC's own product `imageGroups` API field (`overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts`) — an unrelated collision. The most plausible referent is **SFCC-925 "Hero Image Group – PWA Kit Component Build"**, which is **Sprint 7** — a later sprint than SFCC-874's Sprint 6. That trips AGENTS.md Hard Rule 14.
- **The `grid` prop's stated scope contradicts the Figma.** Ticket: *"Grid 3 = 2/3 image width; Grid 4 = 3/4 image width. **Desktop only — no visible difference at tablet/mobile.**"* But in Figma, `Size=Mobile, Grid=3, Qty=2` is **1228.87px** tall and `Size=Mobile, Grid=4, Qty=2` is **1559.75px** tall — a 331px difference on mobile. (Every other mobile/tablet pair does match, so this is one specific disagreement, not a blanket one.)
- **`cardType` has no design.** The Figma component set's variant axes are **Size × Grid × Qty only**. There is no `cardType` axis and no `showTitleAndLink` axis, yet ACs 2–5 depend on both.
- **Three of eighteen Figma variants are not drawn** — see section C.

**3. Which surfaces?** PWA Kit / React **only** for SFCC-874 itself. Contentful is a separate story (and there are currently two competing ones). No SFCC integration: the ticket states *"It does not own the product data or image source — these are passed as props."* PLP is a downstream consumer (SFCC-251), not in scope here.

**4. Design/Figma dependencies?** Yes, unresolved — section C.

**5. API/backend dependencies?** **None for SFCC-874 itself.** Props-in, render-out. The data question is real but lands on SFCC-887/SFCC-920, not here.

**6. Pure FE / shared / needs architecture input?** **Pure FE, but needs one architecture decision first.** The Figma `Size=Desktop|Tablet|Mobile` axis is a design-tool artefact. This codebase does **not** model breakpoints as React props — `ZimmProductCard` has no `size` prop at all (only `variation: 'plp' | 'home' | 'wishlist' | 'recentlyViewed'`; the one `size: string` field is the *product* size on the wishlist variation). Every existing organism handles breakpoints with CSS media queries in its recipe. So AC 10's *"product tiles render below using the Mobile card size"* describes a capability `ZimmProductCard` does not expose. Decide before sizing: does `size` become a real prop (new, contradicts house pattern), or is it CSS-only (cheaper, consistent)?

**7. Sizeable now?** **No.** Sizeable in one refinement pass once Q1–Q4 in section F are answered.

---

## B. The four standing axes

| Axis | State | Ambiguity |
|---|---|---|
| **Behaviour** | Mostly clear | `qty=5` first slot is contradictory. Description: *"four product tiles render in a 2×2 grid alongside the lookbook image **or product**"* — but AC 8 says *"the lookbook image is displayed and 4 product tiles render in a 2x2 grid"*, and SFCC-887 AC 4 says *"Given a Site Merchandiser sets quantity to 5... then the lookbook image field is **not required**."* Three different rules for the same slot. |
| **Desktop/mobile** | Partly clear | Desktop/Tablet/Mobile all have ACs. Tablet `qty=5` was added by comment (14 Sep, Jasmijn Tsang) precisely because no variant is drawn. Unresolved: the mobile Grid=3 vs Grid=4 height contradiction above; and whether `size` is a prop or CSS. |
| **A11y** | Under-specified vs. house standard | ACs say *"passes with no violations"* against **WCAG 2.1 AA**. AGENTS.md targets **WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is infeasible, *with the reason documented*. Also no AC on heading semantics for the section header — SFCC-743 has one (its AC 7), SFCC-874 does not. |
| **Data** | **Unresolved, and contested** | SFCC-874 itself is props-only, which is clean. But the upstream source is genuinely open. `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §1, verbatim: *"PLP / category \| ... \| Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any \| **Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending**"*. And `.docs/memory/projectState.md` lists Contentful as **"Mock — Demo space; not yet Zimmermann's production space."** Worse, the two Contentful stories disagree: SFCC-887 AC 7 says card type *"applies to all tiles in the group"* (group-level); SFCC-920 AC 4 says card type is *"required **per slot**"*. Those cannot both be built. |

---

## C. Design status — evidence

**Designs exist but are incomplete, and the project's own gate for "complete" was not met.**

Figma file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (Zimmermann_Design_System_2026), node **`40000538:25833`**, named **"Group with Lookbok"** (typo is Figma's). It contains **15 variants**. Size × Grid × Qty = 3 × 2 × 3 = **18 expected**. Missing three:

| Breakpoint | Qty=5 drawn at | Missing |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop | Grid=4 only | **Desktop / Grid=3 / Qty=5** |
| Tablet | Grid=3 only | **Tablet / Grid=4 / Qty=5** |
| Mobile | Grid=4 only | **Mobile / Grid=3 / Qty=5** |

The `Qty=5` cell is drawn once per breakpoint at an **inconsistent grid value** — Grid=4 on Desktop and Mobile, Grid=3 on Tablet. So you cannot even infer a "Qty=5 is always Grid=X" rule. This directly contradicts AC 6 and AC 7, which both say *"with **any** qty value."*

This matters because Confluence **04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker** (page `408944644`) sets a hard pre-approval gate, verbatim:

> **Before component user stories are submitted for PO review, confirm the component has ALL variations included in the UI kit.**

> **Hard rule:** Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only.

SFCC-874 was nonetheless approved — Emma Kirwan, 14 Sep: *"hi @... this ticket is approved"* — and moved to `Ready for Development` on 22 Sep by Hazel Marie Cacalda.

**Do not read the Figma link as sign-off.** Confluence **04.7 Component Inventory** (page `400195591`) lists "Product Card Group" as **"🟡 Done, minor update required (confirmed by Dennis)"** — and the PDP template row says *"minor updates needed for PDP Hero and Product Cards Group."*

**A second, separate design problem:** SFCC-743's Design/Technical Notes field points at node **`40000730-13635`** — and **SFCC-925 "Hero Image Group" cites the exact same node**, labelling it *"Component figma (Product Card Group → Hero Image Group)"*. So SFCC-743's link most likely points at the Hero Image Group, not the Product Card Group. The real Product Card Group set is **`40000307:12447`** (inside frame `40000301:11694`, "Product Cards Groups Base") — independently verified in this repo at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts:92`. SFCC-743's link has **already been corrected once** for this exact class of error (Jasmijn, 10 Sep: *"this story was linking out to the search component in DS, not the product card group component. I have updated it with the right link."*).

---

## D. Dependency map

Confluence **04.71 Writing User Stories for Components** (page `400195600`) is the governing pattern. Verbatim:

> **Level 1 — Component epics.** This is the build story for each individual component. It covers what the component does, **its variants and configurations**, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states.

> **Contentful + PWA Kit** (e.g. Banner, Editorial Cards, Footer, Navigation) ... Write **two** stories: One in the **Contentful epic** ... One in the **PWA Kit epic**.

> **Level 2 — Page epics.** ... describe how components work together to deliver a user journey. ... These stories **should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1**.

**The real order:**

```
LEVEL 1 — component                      LEVEL 2 — page consumers
─────────────────────────                ────────────────────────────
SFCC-743  Product Card Group             (sibling, NOT a parent)
          [Tech design, no pts, Sp6]

SFCC-874  Card Group w/ Lookbook  ──┬──► SFCC-251  PLP Bottom Zone   [Tech design, no pts]
          [Ready for Dev, no pts, Sp6]  ├──► SFCC-313  Shop the Edit PDP [Blocked, no pts, Sp7]
                                     └──► SFCC-90   Homepage Modules  [Tech design, no pts]
      ▲

SFCC-887  Contentful content type  ◄──┐  CONFLICT: two competing
          [In Refinement, Squad-B]    ├─ Contentful stories for
SFCC-920  Group w/ Lookbook CF     ◄──┘  one component
          [Tech design, Squad-B]
```

**Does SFCC-874 depend on SFCC-743 shipping first? No.** Evidence:

- **No Jira link exists between them.** SFCC-874's `issuelinks` contains SFCC-313, SFCC-887, SFCC-204, SFCC-251, SFCC-90 — SFCC-743 is absent. Not an oversight to correct; it reflects reality.
- **They are sibling Figma component sets with different variant axes.** SFCC-743 → `40000307:12447`, axes **Size × Display (3/4/6)**. SFCC-874 → `40000538:25833`, axes **Size × Grid (3/4) × Qty (2/3/5)**. Neither nests inside the other.
- **Confluence treats them as separate Modules.** 04.7 lists `Product Card Group | Variants: 3-up, 4-up` and `Product Cards with Lookbook | —` as **two distinct rows**. The lookbook is not listed as a variant of the group.
- **The shared surface is already built.** Both compose `ZimmProductCard` (SFCC-236, merged, `Ready for SIT`, 8 points).

**So: SFCC-874 is a standalone Level 1 component, sizeable independently of SFCC-743.** It is neither additive work on top of it nor a duplicate. The one genuine overlap is the **section header (title + link)**, which neither has built and which does not exist anywhere in the repo — see section E.

**Three real dependency problems this surfaces:**

1. **Two Contentful stories for one component, with contradictory schemas.** Per 04.71 there should be exactly **two** stories total (one Contentful, one PWA Kit). There are three: SFCC-874 + SFCC-887 + SFCC-920. SFCC-887 is group-level `cardType`; SFCC-920 is per-slot. One must be closed or merged.
2. **SFCC-887 mis-attributes the renderer.** Its AC 5 says *"when the PWA Kit component (**SFCC-313**) fetches it"* and its description says *"Rendering is covered in SFCC-313."* But SFCC-313 is a Level 2 PDP page story; SFCC-874 is the component. SFCC-887's own description elsewhere correctly cites SFCC-874. Internally inconsistent.
3. **SFCC-251's placement anchor does not exist.** Its AC 1 says the block renders *"below the **Load More** button."* The PLP renders `<Pagination currentURL={basePath} urls={pageUrls} />` (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:821`). "Load More" exists only as an unused base-SFCC translation string and as a deferred note in `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:385`. Not SFCC-874's problem — but it blocks SFCC-251 from being sized.

## F. Questions for refinement

**Q1 — What is `imageGroup`, and is it SFCC-925?** AC 12 references `imageGroup.showCarousel` / `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator`. Neither is in the props table; neither exists in code. If it means "Hero Image Group" (SFCC-925), that is **Sprint 7** and SFCC-874 is **Sprint 6** — sequencing must change, or the AC must be removed, or the dependency made explicit. → **Jasmijn Tsang (BA) + Bianca Morley (reporter); Marcel to confirm the sprint-order implication.**

Also fix SFCC-887's claim that SFCC-313 is the renderer. → **Jasmijn Tsang (BA) + Squad-B lead; Bianca Morley.**

I have enough to give you defensible numbers. The three deep-dive agents are still running; I'll fold in anything they add.

## First: the premise of your request doesn't hold

You asked me to look at the points you've assigned to see how you approach it. **You have never assigned a story point on this board.**

I checked the changelog on 23 tickets spanning your work and three other squads. Every single value in `customfield_10016` was written by Hazel Cacalda. On your own 19 pointed tickets, your changelog entries are only `duedate`, `status`, `Rank`, `summary`, `description`.

That includes the two you sent me:
- **SFCC-749 → 5**, set by Hazel 2026-09-07, never revised
- **SFCC-801 → 3**, set by Hazel 2026-09-08, never revised

So there's no personal pattern to match. What I built instead is the board's own calibration ladder from shipped work.

## The board's real ladder

| Band | What sits there |
|---|---|
| **3** | One self-contained component reusing an existing shell: `country-language-mismatch` (831), `Logo Masthead` (747), `pdp/hero` (723), `searchfield` (818), `search-open` (819), `suggestion-list` (845) |
| **5** | Drawers and slide-outs, multi-state surfaces: `pdp/drawer` (736), `drawer/content/filters` (847), `Size Guide slide-out` (1023), `Details & Care` (195), `Find in Boutique` (297), `Filters & Facets UI` (108) |
| **8** | Shared global components, multi-surface or PWA+Contentful: `Product Card Shared Component` (236), `Footer PWA Kit` (750), `Navigation PWA+Contentful` (746), `PDP Image Gallery` (186) |
| **13** | One instance only: `Global Header UI` (52) |

**Reality check on the 3s.** SFCC-831 was pointed 3 and took you 24 commits across 12–20 Sep, dragging in ZimmDrawer changes, a Contentful uiCopy seeding pipeline and a CodeRabbit rework round. It still shipped defect SFCC-1013. Treat a 3 on a `global/*` drawer as optimistic.

---

## SFCC-801 — country/currency selector

**Currently 3. My call: 5.**

The 3 was almost certainly anchored on SFCC-831, its sibling in the same namespace, same drawer shell, same "doesn't own redirect logic" carve-out. But SFCC-831 is a message with two buttons. This one is not.

What the AC and Figma actually ask for:
- A **region-group accordion** with chevrons and `aria-expanded`, named in the AC as its own atom and confirmed in Figma as `accordion_country-selector-dropdown`
- Country rows with **flag icon**, name, right-aligned currency code
- Current country's group pre-expanded, radio pre-selected
- **Search field** (confirmed present in the Figma tablet frame)
- Conditional language section with radios
- Sticky header + sticky Confirm footer with the list scrolling independently
- Focus trap, arrow-key radio navigation, focus return

[.docs/prd/regional.md:65](.docs/prd/regional.md#L65) backs this: countries grouped by region with currency display and a search field (REG-021), bag-loss warning (REG-022), EU gets EN/FR/IT/ES while others are English-only (REG-023). The ticket carries five REG IDs against SFCC-831's two.

**What keeps it off 8** — SFCC-831 already paid the infrastructure bill:

| Already built | Path |
|---|---|
| `zimmDrawer` atom + stories + tests + css | [ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer) |

Hazel flagged on 2026-09-07 that desktop large/small were missing; Kiera pointed at a drawer template, and that template does exist — `PDP Drawer Template - Small (25%) - Country & Currency Selector`, 1440×1024 with a 402px drawer. But it only shows the **shell** at desktop size with a generic `pdp/drawer` instance. There is no artboard showing the country-selector content composed into the desktop drawer. Someone has to compose those two by hand.

---

## SFCC-749 — breadcrumb and SEO

**Currently 5. My call: hold at 5.** The number is right; the risk is elsewhere.

Good news first: I went in expecting this to be contaminated with the structured-data suite (DMU-037 to 041, all "custom build", BreadcrumbList scope still unconfirmed with Sparro). **It isn't.** That work lives in SFCC-22 "SEO & Analytics & A/B Testing", which per the tracker isn't dev-ready until 2 Nov, Sprint 7/8.

What SFCC-749 actually covers: breadcrumb on every page generated programmatically from route context with `<nav>` + aria-label + ordered list, plus a Contentful-fed SEO text block with READ MORE/READ LESS, locale-aware, focus management on expand/collapse, and reduced-motion support. That's a clean 5.

**Three things that aren't in the number:**

1. **Hard dependency on an unpointed sibling.** The description says it "consumes the Contentful content type defined in SFCC-748." SFCC-748 is in the same Sprint 6, still in Tech design, no points. If that content type doesn't land, half this story can't be built.
2. **An open item sitting in the description text.** "Rules can be applied to control breadcrumb display on certain page types — open item: Dani to share Sparro templates." Unresolved as written.
3. **Two different Figma files.** The UI kit link is `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`, the expanded state is `Zimmermann_Designs`. Your own rule: don't cross-compare those two.

Copy-first also applies here since the base PWA Kit ships a Breadcrumb, so there's a mandatory stop-and-verify step before any functional work.

---

## SFCC-874 — product card group with lookbook

**Currently unpointed. My call: 8.**

This is the largest of the three and the least ready.

The cost driver is the permutation matrix, not the card. `grid` (3, 4) × `qty` (2, 3, 5) × `size` (Desktop, Tablet, Mobile) is up to 18 layouts, times `cardType` (Product, Editorial) and `showTitleAndLink`. Plus a tablet special case where `qty=5` hides the 4th card to avoid an orphaned row. Plus the AC references `imageGroup.showCarousel` and `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator`, so it depends on an image-group/carousel component too.

Board precedent puts it squarely at 8: `Product Card Shared Component` (236) = 8, `PDP Image Gallery` (186) = 8.

Reuse does exist — `zimmProductCard`, `zimmProductCardContent`, `zimmProductCardMedia`, `zimmMediaTile`, `zimmSlideIndicator`, and `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid`/`Rail` as grouping templates — which is why I'm not arguing 13.

**Two problems bigger than the estimate:**

1. **`grep -ri "lookbook" .docs/prd/` returns nothing.** Not one hit across 17 PRD files. "Shop the Look" exists but it's a PDP cross-sell module (PRD-024), a different thing. Per AGENTS.md this is a stop-and-flag, not an assumption to fill.
2. **Its base is in the same sprint and unpointed.** SFCC-743 "Product Card Group" is Sprint 6, Tech design, no points. You'd be building the variant alongside the thing it varies.

---

## Questions for the room

**For Hazel (delivery):**
- Will these three get companion `: Development` tasks like the Cart stories did on 21 Sep? Right now none of them do, and that changes what the story-level number means.
- SFCC-743 and SFCC-748 are both in Sprint 6, both unpointed, and both block one of these. Intentional?

**For Jas (BA, Regional + PWA Components):**
- SFCC-801: does the country list cover the 11 configured storefronts, or every shippable country? `countries.ts` models 11, each with one currency. A search field over 11 rows is odd, which makes me think the designer expected more.
- SFCC-874: there is no lookbook requirement in the PRD. Which confirmed requirement does this trace to?

**For Kiera / Hannah (design):**
- SFCC-801: is there a composed desktop artboard, or do we compose the tablet content into the Small (25%) template ourselves?
- SFCC-874: `size` is specced as a prop with Desktop/Tablet/Mobile values. Our components do responsive via media queries off `BP`, not a size prop. Is the prop a Figma-variant artifact or a real API requirement?

**For you as FED lead:**
- SFCC-801 needs flag icons. Per the icons rule, if they're not in `overrides/app/components/icons` we ask rather than substitute.

**For Dani:** the Sparro breadcrumb display-rule templates named as an open item on SFCC-749.

---

## Readiness calls

|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-801 | 3 | **5** | Yes. Design composition gap is a build note, not a blocker. |
| SFCC-749 | 5 | **5** | Yes, but blocked in practice on SFCC-748 landing. |
| SFCC-874 | – | **8** | Size it, but it should not be "Ready for Development" with no PRD basis and its base story unpointed in the same sprint. |

I've written nothing to Jira.

<result># SFCC-749 — Backlog Refinement Analysis

## A. Seven-point sizing lens

**(1) Front-end impact?** Yes, entirely — PWA Kit component build. Sibling SFCC-748 holds the Contentful schema half.

**(2) Requirement clear enough to size?** **No.** Three independent contradictions:

- **Authoring surface.** AC says Contentful keyed by category ID. `.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md:57` says the opposite, verbatim: *"CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level (DMU-035, partial resolution 2026-05-15): **SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful)."* SFCC-577's own title is *"PLP SEO Copy Content Field (CMS-Editable, **BM-Configurable**)"*.

**(3) Which surfaces?** AC says breadcrumb on **every page**; SEO text on category/sub-category only. But the confirmed functional requirements only cover PDP (PRD-001) and search (SPR-46) — **PLP/category breadcrumb has no confirmed functional requirement**, only a Design Tracker row marked `PENDING` / *"26-06: Missing in design"*. "Every page" is unbounded and unpriced (cart? checkout? account?).

**(4) Design/Figma dependencies?** Design exists and is unusually complete for the SEO block — but see C, the two links disagree and the breadcrumb itself is undrawn.

**(5) API/backend dependencies?** Breadcrumb: **none, data is already there.** SEO text: blocked on SFCC-748 (no points, status Tech design) and on the Contentful-vs-SFCC decision above. If it resolves to SFCC/BM, this becomes a backend dependency that doesn't exist yet.

**(6) Pure FE / shared / architecture input?** **Needs architecture + cross-squad input**, not pure FE — because of the duplicate-ownership problem in F.

**(7) Sizeable now?** **No.** Sizeable after Q1, Q2 and Q3 in section F are answered.

**Behaviour** — Expand/collapse mechanics are contradicted (`not collapsible` vs READ LESS). Single body vs multi-accordion is contradicted (see C). ---

## A. Seven-point sizing lens

**(1) Front-end impact?** Yes, entirely — PWA Kit component build. Sibling SFCC-748 holds the Contentful schema half.

**(4) Design/Figma dependencies?** Design exists and is unusually complete for the SEO block — but see C, the two links disagree and the breadcrumb itself is undrawn.

**(5) API/backend dependencies?** Breadcrumb: **none, data is already there.** SEO text: blocked on SFCC-748 (no points, status Tech design) and on the Contentful-vs-SFCC decision above. If it resolves to SFCC/BM, this becomes a backend dependency that doesn't exist yet.
