- **AC 12 references props that do not exist in the ticket's own props table.** Verbatim: *"Given `size=Desktop`, when the component renders, then `imageGroup.showCarousel` controls carousel visibility and `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator` has no effect."* There is no `imageGroup` prop in the Props-in-scope table. `grep` for `showCarousel`/`showSlideIndicator` across `overrides/` returns **zero hits**. The only `imageGroup` in the codebase is SFCC's own product `imageGroups` API field (`overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts`) — an unrelated collision. The most plausible referent is **SFCC-925 "Hero Image Group – PWA Kit Component Build"**, which is **Sprint 7** — a later sprint than SFCC-874's Sprint 6. That trips AGENTS.md Hard Rule 14.
- **The `grid` prop's stated scope contradicts the Figma.** Ticket: *"Grid 3 = 2/3 image width; Grid 4 = 3/4 image width. **Desktop only — no visible difference at tablet/mobile.**"* But in Figma, `Size=Mobile, Grid=3, Qty=2` is **1228.87px** tall and `Size=Mobile, Grid=4, Qty=2` is **1559.75px** tall — a 331px difference on mobile. (Every other mobile/tablet pair does match, so this is one specific disagreement, not a blanket one.)
- **`cardType` has no design.** The Figma component set's variant axes are **Size × Grid × Qty only**. There is no `cardType` axis and no `showTitleAndLink` axis, yet ACs 2–5 depend on both.
- **Three of eighteen Figma variants are not drawn** — see section C.

**3. Which surfaces?** PWA Kit / React **only** for SFCC-874 itself. Contentful is a separate story (and there are currently two competing ones). No SFCC integration: the ticket states *"It does not own the product data or image source — these are passed as props."* PLP is a downstream consumer (SFCC-251), not in scope here.

**4. Design/Figma dependencies?** Yes, unresolved — section C.

**5. API/backend dependencies?** **None for SFCC-874 itself.** Props-in, render-out. The data question is real but lands on SFCC-887/SFCC-920, not here.

**6. Pure FE / shared / needs architecture input?** **Pure FE, but needs one architecture decision first.** The Figma `Size=Desktop|Tablet|Mobile` axis is a design-tool artefact. This codebase does **not** model breakpoints as React props — `ZimmProductCard` has no `size` prop at all (only `variation: 'plp' | 'home' | 'wishlist' | 'recentlyViewed'`; the one `size: string` field is the *product* size on the wishlist variation). Every existing organism handles breakpoints with CSS media queries in its recipe. So AC 10's *"product tiles render below using the Mobile card size"* describes a capability `ZimmProductCard` does not expose. Decide before sizing: does `size` become a real prop (new, contradicts house pattern), or is it CSS-only (cheaper, consistent)?

**7. Sizeable now?** **No.** Sizeable in one refinement pass once Q1–Q4 in section F are answered.

---

## B. The four standing axes

| Axis | State | Ambiguity |
|---|---|---|
| **Behaviour** | Mostly clear | `qty=5` first slot is contradictory. Description: *"four product tiles render in a 2×2 grid alongside the lookbook image **or product**"* — but AC 8 says *"the lookbook image is displayed and 4 product tiles render in a 2x2 grid"*, and SFCC-887 AC 4 says *"Given a Site Merchandiser sets quantity to 5... then the lookbook image field is **not required**."* Three different rules for the same slot. |
| **Desktop/mobile** | Partly clear | Desktop/Tablet/Mobile all have ACs. Tablet `qty=5` was added by comment (14 Sep, Jasmijn Tsang) precisely because no variant is drawn. Unresolved: the mobile Grid=3 vs Grid=4 height contradiction above; and whether `size` is a prop or CSS. |
| **A11y** | Under-specified vs. house standard | ACs say *"passes with no violations"* against **WCAG 2.1 AA**. AGENTS.md targets **WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is infeasible, *with the reason documented*. Also no AC on heading semantics for the section header — SFCC-743 has one (its AC 7), SFCC-874 does not. |
| **Data** | **Unresolved, and contested** | SFCC-874 itself is props-only, which is clean. But the upstream source is genuinely open. `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §1, verbatim: *"PLP / category \| ... \| Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any \| **Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending**"*. And `.docs/memory/projectState.md` lists Contentful as **"Mock — Demo space; not yet Zimmermann's production space."** Worse, the two Contentful stories disagree: SFCC-887 AC 7 says card type *"applies to all tiles in the group"* (group-level); SFCC-920 AC 4 says card type is *"required **per slot**"*. Those cannot both be built. |

---

## C. Design status — evidence

**Designs exist but are incomplete, and the project's own gate for "complete" was not met.**

Figma file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (Zimmermann_Design_System_2026), node **`40000538:25833`**, named **"Group with Lookbok"** (typo is Figma's). It contains **15 variants**. Size × Grid × Qty = 3 × 2 × 3 = **18 expected**. Missing three:

| Breakpoint | Qty=5 drawn at | Missing |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop | Grid=4 only | **Desktop / Grid=3 / Qty=5** |
| Tablet | Grid=3 only | **Tablet / Grid=4 / Qty=5** |
| Mobile | Grid=4 only | **Mobile / Grid=3 / Qty=5** |

The `Qty=5` cell is drawn once per breakpoint at an **inconsistent grid value** — Grid=4 on Desktop and Mobile, Grid=3 on Tablet. So you cannot even infer a "Qty=5 is always Grid=X" rule. This directly contradicts AC 6 and AC 7, which both say *"with **any** qty value."*

This matters because Confluence **04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker** (page `408944644`) sets a hard pre-approval gate, verbatim:

> **Before component user stories are submitted for PO review, confirm the component has ALL variations included in the UI kit.**

> **Hard rule:** Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only.

SFCC-874 was nonetheless approved — Emma Kirwan, 14 Sep: *"hi @... this ticket is approved"* — and moved to `Ready for Development` on 22 Sep by Hazel Marie Cacalda.

**Do not read the Figma link as sign-off.** Confluence **04.7 Component Inventory** (page `400195591`) lists "Product Card Group" as **"🟡 Done, minor update required (confirmed by Dennis)"** — and the PDP template row says *"minor updates needed for PDP Hero and Product Cards Group."*

**A second, separate design problem:** SFCC-743's Design/Technical Notes field points at node **`40000730-13635`** — and **SFCC-925 "Hero Image Group" cites the exact same node**, labelling it *"Component figma (Product Card Group → Hero Image Group)"*. So SFCC-743's link most likely points at the Hero Image Group, not the Product Card Group. The real Product Card Group set is **`40000307:12447`** (inside frame `40000301:11694`, "Product Cards Groups Base") — independently verified in this repo at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts:92`. SFCC-743's link has **already been corrected once** for this exact class of error (Jasmijn, 10 Sep: *"this story was linking out to the search component in DS, not the product card group component. I have updated it with the right link."*).

---

## D. Dependency map

Confluence **04.71 Writing User Stories for Components** (page `400195600`) is the governing pattern. Verbatim:

> **Level 1 — Component epics.** This is the build story for each individual component. It covers what the component does, **its variants and configurations**, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states.

> **Contentful + PWA Kit** (e.g. Banner, Editorial Cards, Footer, Navigation) ... Write **two** stories: One in the **Contentful epic** ... One in the **PWA Kit epic**.

> **Level 2 — Page epics.** ... describe how components work together to deliver a user journey. ... These stories **should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1**.

**The real order:**

```
LEVEL 1 — component                      LEVEL 2 — page consumers
─────────────────────────                ────────────────────────────
SFCC-743  Product Card Group             (sibling, NOT a parent)
          [Tech design, no pts, Sp6]

SFCC-874  Card Group w/ Lookbook  ──┬──► SFCC-251  PLP Bottom Zone   [Tech design, no pts]
          [Ready for Dev, no pts, Sp6]  ├──► SFCC-313  Shop the Edit PDP [Blocked, no pts, Sp7]
                                     └──► SFCC-90   Homepage Modules  [Tech design, no pts]
      ▲
      │ blocks
SFCC-887  Contentful content type  ◄──┐  CONFLICT: two competing
          [In Refinement, Squad-B]    ├─ Contentful stories for
SFCC-920  Group w/ Lookbook CF     ◄──┘  one component
          [Tech design, Squad-B]
```

**Does SFCC-874 depend on SFCC-743 shipping first? No.** Evidence:

- **No Jira link exists between them.** SFCC-874's `issuelinks` contains SFCC-313, SFCC-887, SFCC-204, SFCC-251, SFCC-90 — SFCC-743 is absent. Not an oversight to correct; it reflects reality.
- **They are sibling Figma component sets with different variant axes.** SFCC-743 → `40000307:12447`, axes **Size × Display (3/4/6)**. SFCC-874 → `40000538:25833`, axes **Size × Grid (3/4) × Qty (2/3/5)**. Neither nests inside the other.
- **Confluence treats them as separate Modules.** 04.7 lists `Product Card Group | Variants: 3-up, 4-up` and `Product Cards with Lookbook | —` as **two distinct rows**. The lookbook is not listed as a variant of the group.
- **The shared surface is already built.** Both compose `ZimmProductCard` (SFCC-236, merged, `Ready for SIT`, 8 points).

**So: SFCC-874 is a standalone Level 1 component, sizeable independently of SFCC-743.** It is neither additive work on top of it nor a duplicate. The one genuine overlap is the **section header (title + link)**, which neither has built and which does not exist anywhere in the repo — see section E.

**Three real dependency problems this surfaces:**

1. **Two Contentful stories for one component, with contradictory schemas.** Per 04.71 there should be exactly **two** stories total (one Contentful, one PWA Kit). There are three: SFCC-874 + SFCC-887 + SFCC-920. SFCC-887 is group-level `cardType`; SFCC-920 is per-slot. One must be closed or merged.
2. **SFCC-887 mis-attributes the renderer.** Its AC 5 says *"when the PWA Kit component (**SFCC-313**) fetches it"* and its description says *"Rendering is covered in SFCC-313."* But SFCC-313 is a Level 2 PDP page story; SFCC-874 is the component. SFCC-887's own description elsewhere correctly cites SFCC-874. Internally inconsistent.
3. **SFCC-251's placement anchor does not exist.** Its AC 1 says the block renders *"below the **Load More** button."* The PLP renders `<Pagination currentURL={basePath} urls={pageUrls} />` (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:821`). "Load More" exists only as an unused base-SFCC translation string and as a deferred note in `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:385`. Not SFCC-874's problem — but it blocks SFCC-251 from being sized.

---

## E. Codebase reality

### (i) Exists and is reusable

| What | Path | State |
|---|---|---|
| **Product card** | `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/` | **Built and merged** (SFCC-236, 8 pts, `Ready for SIT`). 713-line `index.tsx`, 678-line recipe, 1436-line test suite. Four variations: `plp` / `home` / `wishlist` / `recentlyViewed`. Composes `ZimmProductCardMedia` + `ZimmProductCardContent`. Supports `priority` (LCP eager-load) and `imageWidths`. |
| **Card sub-components** | `ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/`, `zimmProductCardContent/`, `zimmProductBadges/`, `zimmSlideIndicator/`, `zimmSizeChipGroup/` | All built and registered. |
| **Closest layout precedent** | `ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/` | **The single most valuable reference.** A responsive CSS-grid organism over `ZimmProductCard`, 822 lines total across 5 files. Its recipe already derives geometry **from the Product Card Group Figma master**: `GRID_CARD_GAP_DESKTOP = '6rem'` with the comment *"96px — confirmed Figma value, checked at two independent sources (40000301:11694 "Product Card Group" master, Size=Desktop/Display=4, node 40000307:12446...)"*, and `GRID_CONTENT_MAX_WIDTH_DESKTOP = '90rem'` = `(288px x 4 cards) + (96px x 3 gaps)`. |
| **Rail precedent** | `ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` | 980 lines. Horizontal-scroll sibling. |
| **Shared card constants** | `ui-kits/zimmProductCardShared.ts` | `CARD_SLOT`, `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`. |
| **Contentful data path** | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts`, `useContentfulClient.ts` | Established. Pattern: `useContentfulEntries<T>(contentType, preview, locale)`. Live consumers: `ui-kits/organisms/zimmBenefits/index.tsx:25`, `components/uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:25`, `components/footer/index.tsx:212`, `hooks/useHeaderNav.ts:53`. |
| **Grid foundation** | `overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts` | `breakpoints` (md 768px, xl 1280px), `grid.columns = { base: 4, md: 8, xl: 10 }`, `containerPadding`, `maxWidth: 'none'`. |

### (ii) Must be built from scratch

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| **`ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCardGroupWithLookbook/`** | Does not exist. `grep -ril "lookbook\|cardgroup\|card-group\|productgroup" overrides/` returns exactly **one** hit — the phrase *"frames' own card-group children"* inside a comment in `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts`. No component, no recipe, no story, no test. |
| **The asymmetric two-zone layout engine** | This is the real cost, and it is **not** analogous to `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid`. That grid is uniform `repeat(N, minmax(0, 1fr))`. SFCC-874 needs a lookbook slot at a 2/3-vs-3/4 width ratio plus a tile column that becomes a **2×2 sub-grid at qty=5**, across three breakpoints, with tablet card-hiding. |
| **Section header (title + link)** | **No shared section-header component exists** — `grep -ril "sectionheader\|section-header" overrides/app/components/` returns nothing. `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid` has a private `header` recipe part, not a reusable component. Needed by SFCC-743 **and** SFCC-874. Possible overlap with SFCC-820 `search/section-header-container` (Squad-B, 5 pts, Sprint 6) — worth checking before both squads build one. |
| **Contentful content type** | `ls scripts/contentful/content-types/` → `footerConfig, headerNavItem, headerNavigation, iconAndText, iconAndTextItem, image, link, navGroup, region, uiCopy`. **No lookbook, no cardGroup, no productCardGroup.** |
| **Studio Experiences registration** | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` is literally `defineComponents([])`, with the comment *"Currently hand-restored as an empty registration: every experiences/\*.tsx component was removed."* Zero registered components. |
| **PLP bottom zone** | No insertion point. `overrides/app/pages/product-list/partials/` contains only `category-links.tsx`. |

### PLP grid — the placeholder claim, verified

**Still true, and the shape is slightly different from how it's usually described.** `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:739`, verbatim:

```tsx
<SimpleGrid columns={[2, 2, 4, 5]} spacingX={4} spacingY={{ base: 12, lg: 16 }}>
```

This is base-SFCC scaffolding, not the Zimmermann grid:
- **5 columns at `lg`+**, where the confirmed Zimmermann desktop grid is **4 columns at 288px**.
- `spacingX={4}` is a **bare Chakra token** (16px), against a confirmed Figma desktop gap of **96px** — and bare token keys are exactly what `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 forbids.
- At the `lg` band (992–1280px) five columns yields roughly **~190–200px per card** — hence the "~200px" symptom. The card itself is width-agnostic by design (`zimmProductCard.css.ts` sets no width), so the width comes entirely from this grid.

Worth noting the two are formally linked in a comment at `index.tsx:123`: *"Derived directly from this file's own `SimpleGrid columns={[2, 2, 4, 5]}`... Update this alongside the SimpleGrid's own `columns` prop if that ever changes."* — `PLP_IMAGE_WIDTHS` will need updating whenever the grid is fixed.

### `.zimm-grid` — available but not a card grid

`overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts:348` registers `.zimm-grid`, but it is **padding-only** (`paddingInline: var(--zimm-grid-margin-mobile|tablet|desktop)`). It provides outer container margins, not column tracks. Per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, global-class adoption is *"currently near zero... none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo."* **A card group cannot get its column layout from `.zimm-grid`** — it must define its own tracks, as `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid` does.

### Nothing started

`git branch -a | grep -i "743\|874\|card.group\|lookbook"` → none. `git log --all --grep="SFCC-743\|SFCC-874"` → none.

---

## F. Questions for refinement

**Q1 — What is `imageGroup`, and is it SFCC-925?** AC 12 references `imageGroup.showCarousel` / `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator`. Neither is in the props table; neither exists in code. If it means "Hero Image Group" (SFCC-925), that is **Sprint 7** and SFCC-874 is **Sprint 6** — sequencing must change, or the AC must be removed, or the dependency made explicit. → **Jasmijn Tsang (BA) + Bianca Morley (reporter); Marcel to confirm the sprint-order implication.**

**Q2 — Draw the three missing Qty=5 variants, or narrow the ACs.** Missing: Desktop/Grid=3/Qty=5, Tablet/Grid=4/Qty=5, Mobile/Grid=3/Qty=5. ACs 6 and 7 currently claim *"any qty value"*. Either the designs come, or `qty=5` is constrained to one `grid` value per breakpoint (and note Figma is currently inconsistent about which). → **Kiera Rikard-Bell / DDP design team** (Confluence 1.5: *"DDP team owns design production... Accenture builds to signed-off designs only"*).

**Q3 — Is `grid` really desktop-only?** Figma shows Mobile/Grid=3/Qty=2 at 1228.87px vs Mobile/Grid=4/Qty=2 at 1559.75px. Either the ticket's *"no visible difference at tablet/mobile"* is wrong, or that Figma variant is. → **Kiera Rikard-Bell + Jasmijn Tsang.**

**Q4 — SFCC-887 or SFCC-920? One must go.** Both are Contentful stories for this component, both Squad-B, both in epic SFCC-304, with **contradictory** card-type models (group-level vs per-slot). 04.71 mandates exactly one Contentful story per component. Also fix SFCC-887's claim that SFCC-313 is the renderer. → **Jasmijn Tsang (BA) + Squad-B lead; Bianca Morley.**

**Q5 — Is `size` a React prop or CSS breakpoints?** `ZimmProductCard` has no `size` prop; every existing organism handles breakpoints in its recipe. AC 10's *"Mobile card size"* assumes a capability that does not exist. Affects SFCC-743 identically. → **Marcel (FED Lead) — tech-design call, and the answer should be written into both tickets.**

**Q6 — Does `cardType=Editorial` reuse SFCC-899's editorial card?** SFCC-899 "Editorial Card Group" (Sprint 7, unpointed, own Figma node `2083-54536`) defines an editorial card with title / image / caption heading / caption description / CTA. SFCC-874 AC 5 says only *"the lookbook slot displays an editorial/campaign image"* — an image, not a card. But SFCC-920 ACs 5–6 describe full editorial cards with header, body copy and link. → **Jasmijn Tsang + Squad-B.**

**Q7 — Who builds the section header, and is it SFCC-820?** No shared section-header component exists. SFCC-743, SFCC-874 and possibly SFCC-820 (`search/section-header-container`, Squad-B, 5 pts, Sprint 6) all need one. → **Marcel + both squad leads.**

**Q8 — Squad ownership.** SFCC-874 is the **only** ticket in epic SFCC-2 labelled both `Squad-A` **and** `Squad-B`. Its Contentful counterparts are Squad-B; SFCC-743 is Squad-A. AGENTS.md Hard Rule 10 requires confirming scope before spanning boundaries. → **Both squad leads.**

**Q9 — WCAG 2.1 or 2.2?** ACs say 2.1 AA; AGENTS.md targets 2.2 AA with documented fallback. Also add a heading-semantics AC to match SFCC-743's AC 7. → **Marcel + Lead QA.**

**Q10 — Is `qty=5` lookbook slot an image, a product, or optional?** Three conflicting statements across SFCC-874's description, SFCC-874 AC 8, and SFCC-887 AC 4. → **Jasmijn Tsang.**

**Q11 — Does PLP editorial come from Contentful at all?** `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` §1 marks this **pending**, and Contentful is still a mock demo space per `projectState.md`. Affects SFCC-251/SFCC-920 more than SFCC-874, but it is the reason the data axis cannot be closed. → **Integration team; Zimmermann merchandising.**

---

## G. Readiness call

**Not ready. Should not carry a point value yet, and arguably should not be in `Ready for Development`** — the project's own Definition of Ready (Confluence `313589763`) states verbatim: *"**Estimated** — Story points have been assigned during backlog refinement using Planning Poker. **Stories with no estimate are not Ready and will not enter planning.**"* SFCC-874's DoR checklist has "Estimated" **ticked**, yet `customfield_10016` is **null** and `jira_batch_get_changelogs` shows a story-point value has **never** been set. Recommend: move back to `Tech design`, resolve Q1–Q5, then size. Q1 (the Sprint-7 `imageGroup` reference) and Q4 (two competing Contentful stories) are the two that could move it out of Sprint 6 entirely.

**Sizing context for when it is ready** — epic SFCC-2 precedent: `SFCC-236` Product Card **8** · `SFCC-820` section-header-container **5** · `SFCC-736` pdp/drawer **5** · `SFCC-847` drawer/filters **5** · `SFCC-731` pdp/gallery **5** · `SFCC-801` **3** · `SFCC-723` pdp/hero **3** · `SFCC-818`/`819`/`845`/`846` **3** each · `SFCC-737` **2** · `SFCC-741` **2** · `SFCC-742` **1**. The closest built analogue, `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid`, is 822 lines across 5 files for a *uniform* grid; SFCC-874's layout is materially harder. **17 of 34 tickets in epic SFCC-2 are unpointed**, so this is not an isolated lapse.

---

## H. What I could not check

1. **The Figma designs visually.** I read the variant *matrix* via `get_metadata` (node names, sizes, positions) — enough to prove which variants exist and to catch the mobile height discrepancy. I did **not** render screenshots or call `get_design_context`, so I cannot speak to spacing values, typography, or whether a drawn variant is internally correct. `get_metadata` on node `40000730:13635` (SFCC-743's / SFCC-925's shared node) **failed with an SSE parse error** — that node's structure is unverified, so my read that it is the Hero Image Group rests on SFCC-925's own field label, not on direct inspection.
2. **The two Jira attachment images** — `image-20260914-013641.png` (SFCC-874) and `image-20260914-015517.png` (SFCC-743). Both are cited in the tablet-behaviour comments and may contain layout detail not in the text.
3. **Whether SFCC-743's Figma link is wrong.** Strongly suggested (same node as SFCC-925; the real master is `40000307:12447`), but not proven — see item 1.
4. **The live Contentful space.** I read `scripts/contentful/content-types/` in code only. Per memory, test/sit/uat hold 38 entries and code defines 6 of 19 live types, so a lookbook type could exist in Contentful without being in code. Not verified this session.
5. **SFCC-204, SFCC-90, SFCC-252, SFCC-928, SFCC-80, SFCC-118, SFCC-314** — read only as link summaries, not in full. SFCC-204 (`PLP – Inline Grid Insert — Contentful`, `Ready For Review`) is the most likely to overlap SFCC-925/SFCC-874.
6. **No Confluence page documents the Zimmermann responsive grid.** Confirmed absent, not merely unfound: searches for `288px`, `gutter`, `grid system`, `card width`, `products per row`, plus a sweep of all 334 page titles, returned nothing. The grid exists **only** in Figma and in this repo's own reverse-engineered `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts` comments. Likewise **no story-point sizing scale is documented anywhere** — only "use Planning Poker" (DoR) and "story is sized and estimated here" (Story Workflow, `247922696`).
7. **`.claude/rules/squadA.md` / `squadB.md`** are drafts and make no claim on `ui-kits/organisms/`, so squad ownership of this component is genuinely undefined in the repo — hence Q8.
8. **`npx tsc --noEmit` / `npm run test` not run** — no code was touched; read-only investigation.</result>

<result>## SFCC-801 — Confluence research report (read-only; nothing written)

**Important tool limitation, stated up front:** the Confluence MCP returns empty `created`/`updated` fields and no author for every page in this space. I can report **version numbers** (reliable) and any **self-declared date/author in the page body**, but I cannot report true last-modified timestamps or last authors. Treat every "date" below as in-body text, not metadata.

---

### 1. The named page — 255852545 "Country List per Storefront" (v7)

Parsed from raw storage XHTML, not eyeballed.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Complete country→storefront mapping? | **Yes.** 203 data rows, 3 columns: `Country \| Region \| Region Site`. Every row is populated. |
| How many countries? | **203 rows / 202 distinct countries.** Australia appears **twice**: `Australia (Default) → Oceania → Australia (AU)` and `Australia → Asia / Oceania → Hong Kong (International)`. |
| **Currency per country?** | **NO. Zero currency data.** Text-only scan of the full storage XHTML: 0 matches for "currenc", and no ISO-4217 codes anywhere. This page **cannot** satisfy the AC requiring a currency code beside each country. |
| **Region groupings?** | **Yes** — a `Region` column with 6 values: Africa 43, Americas 41, Asia / Oceania 30, Europe 59, Middle East 10, Oceania 20. Note these are **geographic** groupings, distinct from the `Region Site` (storefront) column. |
| **Languages per storefront?** | **NO.** 0 matches for "locale", "language", "English". |
| Currency of this page | Version 7. Body says the data was *"extracted from the Zimmermann Global Market Proposition Overview June 2026."* Search-index snippets show version-comment text not present in the body — *"Updated storefront count from 7 to 8 to reflect US Domestic/US International split"* and *"Fixed US + Puerto Rico to US (Domestic); was incorrectly listed as US (International)"* — so it has been maintained past the 8-storefront split. No page comments (0). |

`Region Site` distribution: Australia (AU) 20 · Europe (Domestic) 28 · Europe (International) 73 · Hong Kong (International) 30 · Middle East (International) 10 · UK (Domestic) 1 · US (Domestic) 2 · US (International) 39.

---

### 2. Where the currency data actually lives — and it contradicts itself

**458096644 "International Storefronts and Currencies by Region" (v2)** — `Country | Region site | Storefront type | Currency | D&T message`. 203 rows. This is the only page pairing country with a display currency **and** a storefront.

**466059284 "Global Market Pricing & FX Approach by Country" (v3)** — sectioned per storefront (AU 20, UK 1, US-Dom 2, EU-Dom 30, EU-Intl 71, HK 30, ME 10, US-Intl 39 = 203), columns `Country | ISO | Target Currency | Pricing & FX Approach | ...`. **Only page carrying ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes.**

**These two disagree on currency for roughly half of all markets.** 458096644 assigns a distinct local currency to only ~35 of 203 rows and defaults the rest to the storefront base currency; 466059284 gives nearly every Global-e market its own local target currency. Verified examples:

- Albania EUR vs **ALL** · Algeria EUR vs **DZD** · Azerbaijan EUR vs **AZN** · Benin EUR vs **XOF** · Gibraltar EUR vs **GBP** · Iceland EUR vs **ISK** · Serbia EUR vs **RSD**
- China USD vs **CNY** · Indonesia USD vs **IDR** · Vietnam USD vs **VND** · Cambodia USD vs **KHR**
- Argentina USD vs **ARS** · Chile USD vs **CLP** · Colombia USD vs **COP** · Anguilla USD vs **XCD**

(My manual tally is ~99 of 203 rows disagreeing; treat the exact figure as unverified — the structural disagreement is certain.)

The ME block (10/10) and all domestic blocks agree.

---

### 3. Verbatim requirements for selector behaviour

**303104002 "04.1.6 Regional Storefronts" (v14)** — the authoritative requirements page. Header: *"Requirements extracted from Zimmermann Functional Requirements excel, downloaded July 3rd, 2026 after all requirements were confirmed. — source of truth."* All rows below are status **Confirmed**.

> **REG-021** — "The country selector will display available countries grouped by region (e.g. Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with their associated currency and a search field." *(Storefront: ALL (excl. AU))*

> **REG-020** — "The system will present a country selector allowing customers to manually change their shipping country, redirecting them to the appropriate storefront URL if a selection is made"

> **REG-023** — "Country and language selection will be combined within the same selector. For the EU domestic storefront, customers will be able to select their preferred language (English, French, Italian, Spanish). All other storefronts offer English only."

> **REG-022** — "The system will warn customers that changing their location may result in items being removed from their bag."

**AU gating rule (verbatim):**

> **REG-025** — "All storefronts except AU will include the country selector and allow cross-navigation between regional sites. The AU storefront is gated and does not allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites."

> **REG-009** — "The AU storefront is gated; it is accessible to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IP addresses only."

> **REG-027** — "The system will route customers who select **Australia** from the country selector to the HK website."
> **REG-026** — "The system will route customers who select **China** from the country selector to the HK website."

> **REG-024** — "The selected locale will be reflected in the storefront URL (e.g. /fr-eu/, /it-eu/, /en-eu/)."

**302612483 "04.1.12 Price, Currency and Promotions" (v11)** — the currency-source requirements:

> **PRC-14** — "The system will display a country/currency selector allowing the customer to indicate their shipping country; upon selection, the customer will see prices in the currency configured for their selected shipping country." *(Comment: "Country Selector not on AU site")*

> **PRC-36** — "The system will store the target currency that customers see for each shipping country. The country-to-currency mapping must be configurable in SFCC without code deployment."

> **PRC-52** — BM interface to "(a) view the target currency configured for each shipping country, (b) set or change the country-to-currency mapping for a country without code deployment, (c) view a complete list of all configured shipping countries and their currencies."

**This is the key architectural finding:** currency is specified as **SFCC BM-configurable runtime data**, not a static list. Neither Confluence table is the intended source of truth for the selector's currency column.

---

### 4. Other relevant pages

| ID | Title | Ver | What it contains |
|---|---|---|---|
| 486932513 | Global Market Proposition — Country, Region & Terms of Trade | 6 | *"218 markets across 8 storefronts."* Per-storefront sections with Terms of Trade (Domestic / Hidden DDP / DDP / DDU / **Disabled**). 15 markets are **Disabled** (Turkey, Libya, Iran, Iraq, Syria, Yemen, Afghanistan, North Korea, Somalia, Eritrea, Rwanda, Mali, Niger, Central African Republic, Congo-Kinshasa). 218 − 15 = **203**, reconciling with the other three tables. **The selector must exclude the Disabled set.** No currency column. |

Latest in-body note anywhere on the page is 07-07. **Stale** (superseded by the 04.7x component-level trackers). |
| 408944644 | 04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker | 7 | "Regional storefront — Country selector, language modal, currency indicator": design finalised **Aug 24 (Sprint 3)**, stories ready for dev **Sep 7**. Design lead column **blank**. |
| 400195591 | 04.7 Component Inventory | 13 | **No country/region/currency selector component exists in the inventory at all.** The one "Drawer" row reads **"Designs Empty … Incomplete"**. |
| 491126816 | 5.9.2.23 — Region | 3 | Contentful `Region` content type = one entry per SFCC storefront (`siteId`, `label`, `locale`). **Models storefronts, not geographic region groupings** — cannot supply the selector's accordion groups. Only one fixture (`ZimmermannAU`) exists. |
| 340000875 | 11. Multi-Site & Locale Configuration | 3 | BM setup checklist. Says *"seven storefronts"*; **HK is missing from the site-creation list entirely**. "Country-to-site routing logic configured" and "Language switcher…routes to correct locale URLs" both **incomplete**. |

---

### 5. Contradictions to raise in refinement

1. **Currency source is triple-forked.** 255852545 (no currency) vs 458096644 (base-currency-defaulted) vs 466059284 (full local target currency) — and PRC-36/PRC-52 say the real source is BM config, not any of them. **The AC's "currency code next to each country" has no agreed data source today.**
2. **Andorra and San Marino are assigned to different storefronts by different pages.** 255852545 and 486932513 place both in **Europe (International)**; 466059284 places both in **EU-Domestic** (its EU-Dom section is 30, vs 28 on the other two); 458096644 lists both under `Region site` = Europe (Domestic) but gives Andorra `Storefront type` = International — internally inconsistent.
3. **URL prefixes conflict three ways** — critical, because REG-020 requires redirecting to a storefront URL:
   - REG-043 + TSD §5.1: AU = `/`, US domestic = `/us/`
   - 04.5 Storefronts: AU = `/en-au`, US domestic = **root** (`/us` redirects to root)
   - 340000875: examples `/en-AU/`, `/en-GB/`, `/fr-FR/`
4. **Storefront count is stale in places.** REG-001 says *"7 independent storefronts"* with a comment *"Confirmed 8 storefronts"*; REG-043 says *"11 active locales across 7 storefronts"* then lists 8; 340000875 says seven and omits HK.
5. **Placement/form of the component is described four different ways** — "right-anchored slide-in drawer" (SFCC-801), *header* selector (HPC-026), *page* (04.2 Design Tracker), *footer* flag/locale selector (SFCC-49 TSD §6), and *page template* (04.1.18).
6. **REG-039 vs PRC-14.** REG-039: *"single currency per domestic storefront. No multi-currency toggle will be available within any domestic storefront."* PRC-14 (scope: ALL): selecting a shipping country changes displayed currency. Needs reconciling for AU/UK/EU-dom/US-dom.
7. **HK/ME currency ambiguity.** TSD §5.1 and 458096644 say HK = HKD, ME = AED; 04.5 says default currency HK = USD, ME = EUR (base pricebook). Both are true at different layers, but the selector needs to know which to display.

### 6. Plainly not in Confluence

- **No page mentions SFCC-801, SFCC-688, SFCC-817 or SFCC-823.** Verified by CQL (`text ~ "SFCC-801"` → 0 results; the same query for `SFCC-49` correctly returns its TSD, so the search works).
- **No TSD, functional design, or wireframe exists for the selector itself.** REG-014–035 is explicitly deferred out of both the PWA TSD and the SFCC-49 TSD, and no page picks it up.
- **No Figma link anywhere** for the country/region selector; the 04.2 tracker's Figma cell is empty and 04.7 has no such component.
- **No defined accordion/region-group ordering, no default-expanded state, no search-field behaviour spec** (match on country name only? currency? ISO code?) — REG-021 names a search field but specifies nothing about it.
- **No spec for what the selector shows on the AU storefront** — REG-025 says AU doesn't include it, but nothing states what AU shoppers see instead.</result>

## Revised: two of my three calls were wrong

The deep sweeps on SFCC-749 and SFCC-874 came back with things I missed, and I've verified their load-bearing claims myself. The SFCC-801 sweep is still running.

## E. Questions for refinement

**Q1 — Is this a ~9-row storefront picker or a ~203-row country picker? (BA + designer, jointly — blocking)**
The design lists `EUROPEAN UNION` as a row, which is a storefront, not a country. Confluence 255852545 has 203 country rows. REG-021's search field only makes sense over the long list. This one answer swings flag count from ~9 to ~200 and decides whether search/filter is real work.

**Q2 — What is the source of truth for the currency shown beside each country? (architect + integration — blocking)**
Three Confluence tables disagree (255852545 has none; 458096644 base-currency-defaults ~168 rows; 466059284 gives local currencies) and PRC-36/PRC-52 say it must be **BM-configurable without code deployment**. Is there an API contract, or is this a static FE table for MVP? Related: config says HK=USD/ME=EUR, PRD says HKD/AED.

**Q3 — Which region taxonomy is correct? (BA + designer)**
Figma shows 5 (North America / Europe / Asia-Oceania / Africa / Middle East); REG-021 says 3 ("e.g."); Confluence 255852545 has 6. **Where does South America go?** And what is the group ordering?

**Q4 — Is the language selector always visible or revealed after picking an EU country? (BA)**
SFCC-801's `showLanguageSelector` prop vs SFCC-688 AC#4's sequential step vs Figma's `Step=` variant property. Also: the design shows all four languages while `UNITED KINGDOM` is selected, which contradicts REG-023 ("all other storefronts offer English only").

**Q5 — What does `CLEAR` do, and is `APPLY` disabled until a change is made? (BA + designer)**
`CLEAR` appears in the design and in **no** acceptance criterion.

**Q6 — Is there an AU variant of this component, and what do AU shoppers see instead? (designer + BA)**
Both Figma node names say *"All storefronts except AU"*. REG-025 says AU excludes the selector; nothing says what replaces it. SFCC-688 AC#1 says AU shows country+currency **non-selectable** — that is a read-only mode SFCC-801's AC does not cover.

**Q7 — Flags: confirmed required, and who supplies the assets? (designer + integration)**
Zero exist. The webpack SVG gotcha rules out `<img src>`. If ~200 are needed, is a licensed sprite/CDN acceptable, or does a package need integration-team approval (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7)?

**Q8 — Sticky footer, or inline? (designer)**
AC says the Confirm footer stays sticky with independent list scroll; the desktop template renders the buttons inline directly under the last group with empty space below.

**Q9 — Which default accordion state is correct? (designer)**
The two Figma nodes disagree (all collapsed vs three expanded); the AC says only the current country's group expands.

**Q10 — Does the selector exclude the 15 Disabled markets? (BA)**
Confluence 486932513 lists Turkey, Iran, North Korea, Afghanistan, Somalia and 10 others as Disabled. No AC mentions exclusion.

**Q11 — Does this story include wiring the footer trigger, or is that SFCC-688? (BA + both squad leads)**
`bottomBar/index.tsx` is Tier 2 Global Shell. Also HPC-026 says **header**, SFCC-49's TSD says **footer**, 04.2 tracker says **page**. Scope boundary is undefined.

**Q12 — Can this ship before SFCC-688/SFCC-817? (BA)** See F.

**Q13 — Which storybook/test context, given AU is the default dev site? (QA)**
AU is `/` and is the one storefront where the component is forbidden.

**Q14 — Was 3 points a team estimate? (BA / squad lead)**
The changelog shows a single edit by one person as part of a mark-ready sweep, with no prior estimate value.

## F. Readiness call

**Not sizeable now — blocked on Q1 (storefront-picker vs 203-country picker) and Q2 (currency source of truth).** Those two alone swing the estimate by roughly an order of magnitude, and Q1 also determines whether the largest unbuilt item (flags) is ~9 assets or ~200. **3 points is defensible only for the ~9-row storefront-picker reading with flags supplied**; it is not credible for the 203-row reading, which adds a dataset transcription, ~200 inlined flag SVGs, a search/filter layer, and an accordion + radio atom that do not exist.

**On sequencing (the question as asked):** SFCC-801 is **ahead of both** named redirect owners and **can ship without them**. SFCC-817 is Sprint **7** (one sprint later), `Ready For Review`, unpointed, assignee Tim Lavelle. SFCC-688 is Sprint 6 (same sprint) but only `Tech design`, unpointed, and **`is blocked by` SFCC-49** (`Country List Configuration`, also `Tech design`, unpointed). The AC's `onConfirm(country, locale)` callback contract — *"the consuming page handles the redirect"* — plus the proven opaque-`target` pattern in `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch` means the component is genuinely decoupled. **What SFCC-801 cannot ship without is SFCC-49's country/currency dataset**, and that dependency is not modelled on this ticket: SFCC-49 `blocks` SFCC-688 but only `relates to` SFCC-801.

If currency must come from BM at runtime, there is an unscoped integration contract here.

**6. Pure FE / shared / architecture input?** **Needs architecture input**, on two counts: where the 203-row country dataset lives (repo constant vs SFCC BM vs Contentful), and whether the selector is a storefront picker or a country picker (below).

**7. Sizeable now?** **No.** See F.

---

## B. Four standing axes

**Behaviour — ambiguous.**
- **Apply vs Confirm vs Clear.** AC uses both names for one control: *"the drawer header and the **Confirm** footer remain sticky"* then *"presses the **Apply** CTA"*. The design shows **two** buttons, `CLEAR` and `APPLY`. **`CLEAR` has no AC at all** — does it reset to the current country, or to no selection (and is `APPLY` then disabled)?
- **Language: prop-driven or sequential step?** SFCC-801 AC: *"rendered with showLanguageSelector=true … a Language section with radio options is rendered below the country list"* — always-visible, static. SFCC-688 AC#4: *"Given a shopper selects a country that maps to the EU Domestic storefront, **when they make that selection, then** a language selector is presented … **before the redirect fires**"* — revealed on selection. The Figma variant carries a **`Step=`** property, implying a stepped flow. These are three different interaction models.
- **Default accordion state disagrees between the two Figma nodes.** Desktop template `40002218:52449` renders **all five groups collapsed**; tablet variant `40002218:39722` renders **three expanded** (North America, Europe, Asia/Oceania). AC says only the group containing the current country expands.
- **Search behaviour entirely unspecified** — match on country name only, or also currency/ISO code? Does it filter within collapsed groups, and do groups auto-expand on match?

**Desktop/mobile — mostly answered.** `ZimmDrawer` already implements the full responsive model. `size="small"` = 25% width with a Figma-confirmed 402px floor (`PANEL_MIN_NARROW`), which is exactly the 402px panel in the desktop template. Mobile collapse is automatic below the tablet breakpoint. **Open:** AC says *"full-width on mobile leaving a small space open at the bottom"* — that bottom gap is the `mobile` variant's `MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP` (58px), but `small` does **not** opt into it (`zimmDrawer.css.ts` comments say the baseStyle defaults to full-height precisely so utility drawers don't inherit the PDP strip). So AC and the existing shell disagree about which variant this is.

**A11y — well specified, genuinely demanding.** AC covers focus trap, arrow-key radio navigation, focus return, `aria-expanded` on groups, dialog accessible name, labelled search field, touch targets. Most of the dialog half comes free from `ZimmDrawer`. The **radiogroup-inside-accordion** pattern is the hard part and has no existing atom. Note the standing `zimmLink.css.ts` `sm`-size 22px-vs-24px touch-target shortfall recorded in `overrideStyling.md` — relevant if country rows use `ZimmLink`.

**Data — the largest risk, unresolved at every layer.**
- **Currency has three conflicting Confluence sources and no agreed owner.** Page 255852545 (the one SFCC-817 cites) has **zero currency data**. Page 458096644 defaults ~168 of 203 rows to the storefront base currency. Page 466059284 gives nearly every Global-e market its own local currency. They disagree on roughly half of all markets (Albania EUR vs ALL, China USD vs CNY, Argentina USD vs ARS, Iceland EUR vs ISK…). PRC-36/52 then say the real source is BM config.
- **The design's own currency column contradicts repo config.** Figma shows `CANADA — CAD $` and `NEW ZEALAND — NZD $`. `config/sites.generated.js` has `ZimmermannUSIntl` (`/en-ca/`) = **USD**, and there is **no NZ site at all** (Oceania is served by AU/AUD).
- **HK/ME conflict:** config + `countries.generated.ts` say HK = USD, ME = EUR; `regional.md` and TSD §5.1 say HKD / AED.
- **Region grouping has three incompatible taxonomies:** Figma shows **5** (North America, Europe, Asia/Oceania, Africa, Middle East); PRD REG-021 says *"e.g. Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas"* (**3**, and "e.g." is illustrative not normative); Confluence 255852545's `Region` column has **6** (Africa, Americas, Asia/Oceania, Europe, Middle East, Oceania). `countries.ts`'s `boutiqueRegion` is a fourth, 6-value set explicitly documented for store-locator filtering. **South America has no home in the Figma set.**
- **15 markets are Disabled** (Confluence 486932513: Turkey, Iran, North Korea, Afghanistan, Somalia…). 218 − 15 = 203. The selector must exclude them; no AC says so.

---

## C. Design status

**A desktop design does exist — the Jira thread's gap was closed administratively, and the outcome is only partly what the closure implies.**

Timeline, reconstructed from comments (AEST) and changelog (UTC):

- `2026-09-07 19:07:41+1000` Hazel: *"The design for desktop large and small are not yet available"*
- `19:07:48` (7s later) Hazel removes **"Design available"** from the DoR checklist
- `19:07:59` Hazel sets status **Tech design → Blocked**
- `19:17:32+1000` Kiera: *"Like all the drawer comps, there are different sizes for desktop, tablet and mobile. Please refer to **these** templates within the design system for all the drawer behaviours. We've shown all the drawer templates 🙂"*
- `23:31:16+1000` (~4h14m later) Hazel appends the drawer-templates link to Design/Technical Notes, then at `23:31:31` **Blocked → Tech design**, at `23:31:38` **re-ticks "Design available"**, at `23:31:46` adds "Technical approach understood / Dependencies identified / Testable"
- `2026-09-08 13:13:47+1000` sets **3 points**; `13:13:50` **→ Ready for Development**

**No comment after 2026-09-07 19:17 exists on the ticket.** Nobody ever stated that a desktop component design was produced. The gap was closed by accepting generic drawer templates as the answer.

**What I independently verified in Figma (tool worked):**

- `40002218:52449` = `PDP Drawer Template - Small (25%) - Country & Currency Selector - All storefronts except AU`, a **1440×1024 desktop frame** containing a 402px right-anchored panel. Screenshotted: it renders the real component — header `COUNTRY SELECT`, description, `Search Location` field, five collapsed region groups, `CLEAR`/`APPLY`. **So a Desktop Small composition genuinely exists.**
- `40002218:39722` = `Size=Tablet, Variant=Regional Storefront - Country & Currency Selector - All storefronts except AU, Step=–`. Screenshotted: expanded groups with flag + country + right-aligned currency, radios (UK pre-selected), a `LANGUAGE` radio section (Français/Italiano/Español/English), `CLEAR`/`APPLY`.
- Desktop content width is **338px** (402px panel − 32px padding each side); tablet content is **342px**. Effectively identical — which is why one content design serves both, and supports Kiera's position.
- **"Desktop Large" is arguably not applicable**: `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own Figma-sourced size table lists *"Desktop Small — 25% — Notify Me, Wishlist, Find in Boutique, **Regional Storefront**, Cookies, Login"*. Regional Storefront is a Desktop Small drawer by design-system definition.

**Still not drawn / not confirmable:**
- **No AU variant seen.** Both node names say *"All storefronts except AU"*, implying a counterpart exists, but I could not enumerate it.
- **The `Step=` property's other values are unknown** — directly relevant to the language-flow question.
- **Figma library search does not surface this component set.** `search_design_system` for "country currency selector" returned only `PLP Bar desktop` and a `WishlistOLD` component, with library assets dated `2026-07-06`. I could reach the canvas nodes but **could not enumerate the full variant matrix**.
- **Confluence has no Figma link for it at all.** Tracker 04.2 (258801666) row "Country / Region Selector" is Design Status **PENDING**, Zimmermann Sign-off **Pending**, **Figma Link column empty**, note *"23-06: is this a WIP?"*. Component Inventory 04.7 (400195591) has **no country/region/currency selector row at all**, and its one "Drawer" row reads *"Designs Empty … Incomplete"*. Tracker 04.72 (408944644) claims design finalised Aug 24 with a **blank design-lead column**.

**The design's biggest signal, and it contradicts the requirements:** the rendered list is a **storefront picker (~9 rows)**, not a country picker. It literally lists `EUROPEAN UNION` as a selectable row with `EURO €` — that is not a country. Yet it carries a search field, which only makes sense over a long list, and Confluence 255852545 holds **203 rows**.

---

## D. Codebase reality

### (i) Already exists and is directly reusable

| Path | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx` | **The whole shell.** Right-anchored slide-in (framer-motion, 300ms, Figma `easing.slides`), Chakra-backed focus trap / initial focus / focus restore / Escape / backdrop-close, ref-counted body scroll lock, independent-scroll content area (`flex:1; overflowY:auto; minHeight:0`), `title` header row + close button, `finalFocusRef`/`initialFocusRef`. Sizes `'large' \| 'tablet' \| 'small' \| 'xLarge' \| 'mobile' \| 'prompt'`. Has `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx` **and** `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts`. |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` | `small` = 25% with `PANEL_MIN_NARROW` 402px floor — **exactly the Figma panel width**. |
| `.docs/temp/SFCC-736-195-drawer-tabs-plan.md` | Names this story as a designed-for consumer: *"**SFCC-801 (global country/currency selector — separate right-anchored drawer, same shape)**"* and *"SFCC-801/742's simple-title-header use case"*. |
| `overrides/app/utils/crossSiteUrl.ts` (+ test) | Cross-site URL builder for the redirect. Already handles base-path/site/locale stripping and drops `refine`. |
| `overrides/app/utils/regionPrefCookie.ts` (+ test) | `zimm-region-pref` cookie. **`countrySuppressedAt` (`c`) is already defined, parsed, serialised and tested — with no production writer yet.** Reserved for SFCC-823. |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` (+ test) | Resolves current site+locale → `CountryConfig`. Handles the en-GB UK/EU collision. |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCountryLanguageMismatch/` (+ S/T) | The sibling REG-014/REG-029 prompt. Establishes the **opaque-`target`** contract: *"never read or interpreted … only ever handed back, unmodified"* — the exact pattern SFCC-801's `onConfirm(country, locale)` should follow. |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmLanguagePrompt/` (+ S/T) | Container prior art: cookie-write-then-hard-navigate ordering, `EU_LANGUAGE_CONFIG`. |
| `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:224`, `zimmSizeChipGroup/` | **House radiogroup pattern** — hand-rolled `role="radiogroup"` + roving tabindex. Two working examples to copy. |
| `zimmButton` (`primary`/`secondary`/`icon`, `fullWidth`, `size="adaptive"`), `zimmIcon` (`chevron-down`), `useUiCopy` | CLEAR/APPLY, accordion chevrons, microcopy with fallbacks. |
| `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` + `countries.generated.ts` | 11 storefront routes with `currency`, `locale`, `sfccSiteId`, `shippingCountry`, `boutiqueRegion`. |

**Inventory:** 23 atoms / 16 molecules / 15 organisms under `ui-kits/`.

### (ii) Must be built from scratch

1. **The country dataset.** Nothing in the repo fits. `countries.ts` = 11 storefront routes. `overrides/app/constants/index.ts`'s `SHIPPING_COUNTRY_CODES` = 33 `{value,label}` entries for the checkout address `<select>`, no currency/region/flag, missing Singapore/Malaysia/Brazil/Nigeria. Confluence 255852545's 203 rows have region + storefront but **no currency**. `regional.md` warns *"routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim"* (Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Martinique etc. route to EU International despite Americas geography).
2. **Flag icons — zero exist.** `find -iname "*flag*"` across the repo returns nothing; `overrides/app/assets/svg/` holds 5 files, all logos/payment marks. And per AGENTS.md's Gotchas, **`<img src>` does not work for a project-owned SVG** — each would need inlining as JSX `<path>` data, a sprite, or a CDN. The gotcha explicitly warns *"this only breaks in the real app build"*, so a green test suite will not catch it. **This is the single largest hidden line item**, and its size swings ~20× on the 9-vs-203 question.
3. **Accordion region group.** No `zimmAccordion`. Chakra's `Accordion*` is reachable only via `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui` — and per the known barrel trap, shadowing that barrel intercepts nothing, so it arrives unstyled.
4. **Radio atom.** No `zimmRadio`. Raw Chakra `Radio` is used in exactly one place (`product-view/index.tsx:1548`, inherited base code).
5. **The boxed search field.** `zimmSearchInput` is **not reusable** — it is the 180×24px underline header search, hardwired to `searchUrlBuilder` + `useNavigation` + recent-search session history. The design needs a 342×44 boxed filter input. This is the recurring `ZimmTextInput` boxed-variant gap.
6. **Search/filter logic** over the list, incl. group auto-expansion on match.
7. **Trigger wiring.** `overrides/app/components/footer/bottomBar/index.tsx` currently has `const LOCALE_LABEL_PLACEHOLDER = 'Australia (AUD) / ENG'` rendered as a **non-interactive `div`**, with the comment *"PLACEHOLDER: wire to locale selector once available … Swap back to a real button with an onClick when the selector lands."* Tier 2, Global Shell, both squads. Also note Confluence HPC-026 puts the selector in the **header**, not the footer.
8. **Theme recipe(s)** + registration in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
9. **AU suppression.** REG-020/REG-025: the selector must not render on AU — which is `defaultSite: 'ZimmermannAU'` at `/`, i.e. the default local-dev and Storybook context.

---

## E. Questions for refinement

**Q1 — Is this a ~9-row storefront picker or a ~203-row country picker? (BA + designer, jointly — blocking)**
The design lists `EUROPEAN UNION` as a row, which is a storefront, not a country. Confluence 255852545 has 203 country rows. REG-021's search field only makes sense over the long list. This one answer swings flag count from ~9 to ~200 and decides whether search/filter is real work.

**Q2 — What is the source of truth for the currency shown beside each country? (architect + integration — blocking)**
Three Confluence tables disagree (255852545 has none; 458096644 base-currency-defaults ~168 rows; 466059284 gives local currencies) and PRC-36/PRC-52 say it must be **BM-configurable without code deployment**. Is there an API contract, or is this a static FE table for MVP? Related: config says HK=USD/ME=EUR, PRD says HKD/AED.

**Q3 — Which region taxonomy is correct? (BA + designer)**
Figma shows 5 (North America / Europe / Asia-Oceania / Africa / Middle East); REG-021 says 3 ("e.g."); Confluence 255852545 has 6. **Where does South America go?** And what is the group ordering?

**Q4 — Is the language selector always visible or revealed after picking an EU country? (BA)**
SFCC-801's `showLanguageSelector` prop vs SFCC-688 AC#4's sequential step vs Figma's `Step=` variant property. Also: the design shows all four languages while `UNITED KINGDOM` is selected, which contradicts REG-023 ("all other storefronts offer English only").

**Q5 — What does `CLEAR` do, and is `APPLY` disabled until a change is made? (BA + designer)**
`CLEAR` appears in the design and in **no** acceptance criterion.

**Q6 — Is there an AU variant of this component, and what do AU shoppers see instead? (designer + BA)**
Both Figma node names say *"All storefronts except AU"*. REG-025 says AU excludes the selector; nothing says what replaces it. SFCC-688 AC#1 says AU shows country+currency **non-selectable** — that is a read-only mode SFCC-801's AC does not cover.

**Q7 — Flags: confirmed required, and who supplies the assets? (designer + integration)**
Zero exist. The webpack SVG gotcha rules out `<img src>`. If ~200 are needed, is a licensed sprite/CDN acceptable, or does a package need integration-team approval (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7)?

**Q8 — Sticky footer, or inline? (designer)**
AC says the Confirm footer stays sticky with independent list scroll; the desktop template renders the buttons inline directly under the last group with empty space below.

**Q9 — Which default accordion state is correct? (designer)**
The two Figma nodes disagree (all collapsed vs three expanded); the AC says only the current country's group expands.

**Q10 — Does the selector exclude the 15 Disabled markets? (BA)**
Confluence 486932513 lists Turkey, Iran, North Korea, Afghanistan, Somalia and 10 others as Disabled. No AC mentions exclusion.

**Q11 — Does this story include wiring the footer trigger, or is that SFCC-688? (BA + both squad leads)**
`bottomBar/index.tsx` is Tier 2 Global Shell. Also HPC-026 says **header**, SFCC-49's TSD says **footer**, 04.2 tracker says **page**. Scope boundary is undefined.

**Q12 — Can this ship before SFCC-688/SFCC-817? (BA)** See F.

**Q13 — Which storybook/test context, given AU is the default dev site? (QA)**
AU is `/` and is the one storefront where the component is forbidden.

**Q14 — Was 3 points a team estimate? (BA / squad lead)**
The changelog shows a single edit by one person as part of a mark-ready sweep, with no prior estimate value.

---

## F. Readiness call

**Not sizeable now — blocked on Q1 (storefront-picker vs 203-country picker) and Q2 (currency source of truth).** Those two alone swing the estimate by roughly an order of magnitude, and Q1 also determines whether the largest unbuilt item (flags) is ~9 assets or ~200. **3 points is defensible only for the ~9-row storefront-picker reading with flags supplied**; it is not credible for the 203-row reading, which adds a dataset transcription, ~200 inlined flag SVGs, a search/filter layer, and an accordion + radio atom that do not exist.

**On sequencing (the question as asked):** SFCC-801 is **ahead of both** named redirect owners and **can ship without them**. SFCC-817 is Sprint **7** (one sprint later), `Ready For Review`, unpointed, assignee Tim Lavelle. SFCC-688 is Sprint 6 (same sprint) but only `Tech design`, unpointed, and **`is blocked by` SFCC-49** (`Country List Configuration`, also `Tech design`, unpointed). The AC's `onConfirm(country, locale)` callback contract — *"the consuming page handles the redirect"* — plus the proven opaque-`target` pattern in `ZimmCountryLanguageMismatch` means the component is genuinely decoupled. **What SFCC-801 cannot ship without is SFCC-49's country/currency dataset**, and that dependency is not modelled on this ticket: SFCC-49 `blocks` SFCC-688 but only `relates to` SFCC-801.

---

1. **Full Figma variant matrix.** `search_design_system` did not return this component set (only `PLP Bar desktop` and `WishlistOLD`; library assets dated 2026-07-06). I reached the two linked canvas nodes and screenshotted both, but **could not enumerate all `Size=` values, confirm whether an AU variant exists, or read the `Step=` property's other values.** I did not run `get_design_context` (heavy, and this is refinement not implementation), so exact tokens/spacing are unverified.

3. **The source spreadsheet.** `regional.md` states the authoritative per-country mapping *"lives in the source sheet"* (`Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx`, "Country to Storefront Mapping"). Not accessible from here.
4. **Whether the desktop template `40002218:52449` is signed off.** It exists and renders, but Confluence tracker 04.2 still shows the selector as Design **PENDING** with an empty Figma-link cell, and 04.7 has no row for it.
5. **Sticky-footer behaviour at overflow.** The desktop screenshot has all groups collapsed, so content never overflows — I could not tell from a static render whether the footer is pinned.
6. **Exact count of disagreeing currency rows** between Confluence 458096644 and 466059284 (~99 of 203 by manual tally — the structural disagreement is certain, the number is not).
7. **`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and `projectState.md` are stale and mention none of these tickets.** sprintScope self-dates 2026-06-23, still says "Sprint 0", calendar ends 11 Sep. projectState last updated 2026-08-24, predates all the shipped SFCC-831/689 regional work. content.text: ## Correcting my SFCC-801 call I gave you **5 with high confidence**. That was overconfident. I'd verified that `zimmDrawer` exists and assumed the rest of the parts did too. They don't. **What I got wrong:** | I said | Actually | |---|---| | `zimmDropdown` is reusable for the country list | It's a listbox-style form select with a floating label and a trigger panel. The AC needs inline region accordions with radio rows. Adjacent machinery, not the component. | | Scaffolding keeps it off 8 | **Zero flag assets exist.** `find -iname "*flag*"` returns nothing; `assets/svg/` holds 5 files, all logos and payment marks. No `zimmRadio`. No `zimmAccordion`. And `zimmSearchInput` is hardwired to the header — its own docstring says *"180×24px underline-style field"*, it imports `searchUrlBuilder` and `useNavigation` and writes session recent-search history. The design needs a 342×44 boxed filter input. | And the flags matter more than they look. Per the AGENTS.md gotcha, `` **does not work** for a project-owned SVG in this build — webpack's `svg-sprite-loader`/`ignore-loader` applies to every `.svg` import. Each flag has to be inlined as JSX path data. Vitest and Storybook both make `` appear to work, so a green suite won't catch it. **The question that decides the number:** the Figma renders roughly **9 rows and lists "EUROPEAN UNION" as one of them** — that's a storefront picker, not a country picker. But REG-021 mandates a search field, and the Confluence source table has **203 country rows**. A search field over 9 rows makes no sense. - **Storefront picker (~9 rows):** 5. Maybe 3. - **Country picker (~203 rows):** dataset transcription, ~200 inlined flag SVGs, a search/filter layer, plus accordion + radio + boxed-input atoms from scratch. **8, arguably 13.** Same order-of-magnitude question I raised earlier, but I under-weighted it. It isn't a refinement nicety — it *is* the estimate. --- ## The actual headline: all three duplicate something This isn't three coincidences. | Story | Duplicates | How you spot it | |---|---|---| | **SFCC-801** | **SFCC-688** "Regional Storefronts — Country & Language Selector" — Squad-A, Sprint 6, Tech design, unpointed | SFCC-688 carries REG-020, 021, 022, 023, **024**, 025, **026**, **027**. A strict superset of SFCC-801's five. | | **SFCC-749** | SFCC-578, 95, 577, 579, 573 — all Squad-B, epic SFCC-22 | Shared DMU-/SPR- labels | | **SFCC-874** | SFCC-887 and SFCC-920 — two competing Contentful stories with contradictory `cardType` models | Both in epic SFCC-304 | Shared requirement-ID labels are the fastest duplication detector on this board, and nobody is running that check. Also worth knowing: **SFCC-49 "Country List Configuration"** (Tim Lavelle, Sprint 6, Tech design, unpointed) is the real dataset dependency for SFCC-801 — and it's linked `relates to`, not `blocks`, so it doesn't render as a blocker anywhere. --- ## Final numbers | Story | Now | Number | Condition | |---|---|---|---| | **SFCC-801** | 3 | **5** or **8** | 5 if it's the ~9-row storefront picker the Figma draws. 8 if it's the 203-row country list REG-021's search field implies. Not sizeable until someone answers that. | | **SFCC-749** | 5 | **5** | Holds for the AC as literally written. 8+ if the Figma's five-accordion design wins. Don't commit either way. | | **SFCC-874** | – | **8** | Ladder-consistent. But AC 12 references SFCC-925, which is Sprint 7. | One thing the 3 on SFCC-801 isn't: a team estimate. Hazel set it at 03:13:47 UTC on 8 Sep, **two seconds** before the DoR checklist auto-ticked "Estimated" and **three seconds** before the status flipped to Ready for Development. That's an administrative sweep. Nothing written to Jira. --- ## What you're missing **The estimate isn't the deliverable here — the duplication is.** You can walk into refinement with 5 / 5 / 8 and be technically correct while the room agrees to build three things twice. Of the two, only one costs a sprint. **SFCC-688 is the one to raise first.** It's yours-adjacent (Hazel's, Squad-A, same sprint), unpointed, and it covers everything SFCC-801 covers plus REG-024, 026, 027. Either SFCC-801 is the component and SFCC-688 is the page-level consumer — which is the Confluence 04.71 Level-1/Level-2 pattern and would make both legitimate — or they're the same story written twice. Nobody has said which, and the labels suggest the second. **The flag assets are a procurement question, not a dev question, and it's yours.** If the answer to Q1 is 203 countries, someone has to source ~200 flag SVGs. Per Hard Rule #7 a licensed sprite package needs integration-team approval. 7. Check .docs/prd/plp.md and .docs/prd/homepage.md for any requirement describing a product card group / grid of N cards with a section header, and quote it with its requirement ID. If none exists, say so plainly.

RETURN:

C. Design status with evidence — which Figma node is authoritative, is the ticket's link correct, are all variants drawn.
D. Codebase reality: (i) exists and reusable with paths and line counts, (ii) must be built from scratch.
E. Duplication/overlap findings — especially SFCC-820 and any shared-label tickets.
F. Specific refinement questions, each tagged with who answers (BA Jasmijn / designer Kiera / architect / integration / QA / Marcel as FED lead).
G. A story-point recommendation against the ladder above, with the reasoning, and a one-line readiness call.
H. What you could NOT check.

Quote evidence verbatim where it matters. Never invent an AC, dependency or estimate — if it is not in the ticket it is a question, not a finding.

content.text:
I have verified positions on both while the deep sweeps run. Here's what I can stand behind now.

## SFCC-743 — Product Card Group

**My number: 5.**

This is the cleanest of the five. Ten ACs, no internal contradictions, and the component is explicitly props-only: *"It does not own the product data or navigation logic — it receives a product array, title, and link label as props."*

**Props:** `display` (3, 4, 6) · `size` (Desktop, Mobile) · `showTitleAndLink` · `showLink` · `title` · `linkLabel`. Plus a tablet addendum: at `display=4`, tablet renders 3 cards and hides the 4th — the same orphan-row rule SFCC-874 uses for `qty=5`.

**Why 5 and not 3:** the calibration anchor is almost exact. The closest built analogue is Recently Viewed — `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid` (822 lines) plus `zimmRecentlyViewedRail` (980 lines), both grids of `ZimmProductCard` with title rows. That work landed under **SFCC-83 (3 pts) + SFCC-917 (2 pts) = 5**, across 36 commits. SFCC-743 is the same shape, generalised. Separately, SFCC-820 `search/section-header-container` is a **5** for the section header *alone*.

**Why not 8:** `ZimmProductCard` is built and shipped (SFCC-236), and there are two working grid/rail precedents to copy.

**The thing that makes this the most important of the five:** it's the only one whose blocker is already satisfied, and it unblocks three other stories.

| SFCC-743 relationship | Ticket | State |
|---|---|---|
| **is blocked by** | SFCC-236 Product Card Shared Component | **Ready for SIT — done** ✅ |
| **blocks** | SFCC-118 Recommendations – Recommended for You | Blocked, Squad-B |
| **blocks** | SFCC-314 Recommendations – More from Category | Blocked, Squad-B |
| **blocks** | SFCC-80 PLP UI – Product Grid Structure | Tech design, **yours** |

SFCC-118 and SFCC-314 are sitting in Blocked right now waiting on it. SFCC-80 is the story that would replace the placeholder `SimpleGrid columns={[2, 2, 4, 5]}` on the PLP — and it's assigned to you.

**One architecture call you'll have to make.** A title-plus-link row now exists twice, built two different ways. The rail has a `title-and-link` recipe part derived from the Figma build plan; the grid has its own title row, and its docblock says explicitly: *"This grid does NOT share its title row with `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title-and-link`."* SFCC-743 would be the third. Extract one, or ship a third variant. Extracting touches two already-shipped components.

---

## SFCC-748 — Breadcrumb and SEO, Contentful

**My number: 3. But I'd argue against building it at all until someone resolves the premise.**

Four ACs, all schema. The content type is: category ID (mandatory), title, intro text, expanded SEO body, locale support. Against the ladder, SFCC-912 *"Footer — Contentful Component: Development & Testing"* was **3**, and the footer content type is richer than this one. So 3 is the ceiling; 2 is arguable.

**The problem is the premise.** SFCC-748's user story reads: *"I want to manage SEO text content in Contentful per category, so that it can be updated per storefront without a code deployment."*

Two confirmed PRDs say that content should not live in Contentful:

- [dataMigrationSeo.md:57](.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md#L57) (DMU-035): *"**SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful). Still Open: Sparro to define field schema before custom build."*
- [plp.md:18](.docs/prd/plp.md#L18) (SPR-03/04, Confirmed 2026-05-08): *"Configurable title, description, and hero image per category page **via Business Manager**."*

And Squad-B's SFCC-577 is titled *"PLP SEO Copy Content Field (CMS-Editable, **BM-Configurable**)"*.

So SFCC-748 and SFCC-577 are the same requirement with opposite answers about where the content lives. Both can't be right, and building the wrong one means building a content type nobody authors into.

Note also that SFCC-748 is labelled `Config`, not `Custom` — the only one of the five labelled that way.

---

## The five together

| Story | Number | Blocker state | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-743** | **5** | **Clear** — SFCC-236 done | Unblocks 3 stories. Build this first. |
| **SFCC-801** | **5** or **8** | SFCC-49 dataset, Tech design | 9-row vs 203-row question decides it |
| **SFCC-749** | **5** | SFCC-748 unresolved | Overlaps 5 Squad-B tickets |
| **SFCC-748** | **3** | Premise contested | May be building the wrong store |
| **SFCC-874** | **8** | SFCC-925 is Sprint 7 | No PRD basis for "lookbook" |

**Sequencing, since you'll be asked:** SFCC-743 first — it's the only one that's genuinely ready, and it releases three blocked stories. Everything else waits on a decision someone else has to make.

Both deep sweeps are still running. Given last round's sweeps changed two of my three calls, treat SFCC-743's 5 and SFCC-748's 3 as provisional until they land — particularly SFCC-743's Figma link, which may point at the Hero Image Group node rather than the Product Card Group master.

---

## What you're missing

**Adding these two didn't reduce the open questions, it added a sixth duplicate.** SFCC-743 has its own Contentful sibling, **SFCC-744 "product-card-group — Contentful"** — To Do, unassigned, no sprint, no points, epic SFCC-304. So the pairing pattern now runs: 743↔744, 749↔748, 874↔887↔920. Three PWA stories, four Contentful stories, and only one of those four (SFCC-748) is in the sprint.

**SFCC-118 and SFCC-314 look like duplicates of each other.** Both "Recommendations", both Squad-B, both Blocked, both `DesignDependent`, and both carry the identical label set SPR-58 / SPR-59 / SPR-62. That's the same signature that flagged the others. Not your tickets, but they're the two SFCC-743 unblocks, so their state is your problem the moment you ship it.

**SFCC-80 is yours, unpointed, and blocked by SFCC-743.** It's the PLP grid fix. You're holding both ends of that chain and neither has a number.

**If I don't hear back:** nothing gets written to Jira and the five stay as they are. When the sweeps land I'll reconcile and flag anything that moves.

# SFCC-748 Backlog Refinement — Analysis

## Headline

**SFCC-748 is not ready, has never been pointed, and its core premise is contradicted by three confirmed sources. It should not be built as written.** The work it describes is also already specced twice elsewhere, by a different squad, in a different epic, with the opposite storage decision.

---

## Ticket state (verbatim)

**SFCC-748** — "Breadcrumb and SEO – Contentful Component" · epic SFCC-3 (Navigation) · status **Tech design** · Sprint 6 · reporter **Isabel Chaloner** · created 2026-08-17 · **labels `["Config", "Squad-A"]`** (note: `Config`, not `Custom` — and **no DMU requirement label**, unlike every Squad-B SEO sibling).

**Story points: never set.** Across all **53 changelog entries** there is not one story-point field change. This isn't "points were removed" — they were never entered.

**Acceptance criteria** (`customfield_10231`, verbatim — 4 ACs):

> \# Given the Contentful content type is created, when a Site Merchandiser opens the content model, then it includes category ID (mandatory), title (optional), intro text (optional), expanded SEO body (optional), and locale support.
> \# Given a Site Merchandiser creates a new entry, when they complete only the category ID field, then the entry is valid and can be published — all other fields are optional.
> \# Given a Site Merchandiser creates or updates a Contentful entry, when they author content for a specific locale, then the content is independently managed per locale and changes to one locale do not affect another.
> \# Given a Site Merchandiser updates and publishes a Contentful entry for a category, when the page loads after publishing, then the updated content is reflected without a code deployment.

**Issue links:** one only — `relates to SFCC-749`. No link to any Squad-B SEO ticket.

**Attachments:** 2 Figma screenshots (`image-20260830-234504.png`, `image-20260830-234554.png`), both uploaded by Isabel Chaloner 2026-08-31.

**Design/Technical Notes:** set 2026-09-15 by Isabel — a Figma Design System 2026 link (`node-id=40007614-112495`).

**Changelog — the churn is the story.** Status went `To Do → In Refinement` (2026-08-17) `→ Ready For Review` (08-31) `→ Tech design` (09-03) `→ Blocked` (09-07) `→ Tech design` (2026-09-22 01:18). Assignee went Marcel → Kiera Rikard-Bell → Hazel Cacalda → **back to Marcel**. Sprint went `None → 6 → 7 → 6`.

**The last four changes all happened within 17 seconds on 2026-09-22 01:18** — assignee to Marcel, sprint back to 6, DoR checklist expanded from 3 items to 7, status unblocked from `Blocked` to `Tech design`. Nothing in the ticket changed substantively; it was administratively unblocked and handed to you.

**Comments — the open question was never answered:**
> Hazel Marie Cacalda (2026-09-07): "can you confirm that the link in the Design field is the final approved version?"
> Isabel Chaloner (2026-09-15): "added"

"Added" answers a different question than "is it approved."

---

## C. THE CENTRAL VERDICT

**Yes — clearly. SFCC-748 builds a Contentful content type that the confirmed PRD says should live in SFCC/Business Manager.** Three independent confirmed sources say BM/SFCC; one unconfirmed Jira story says Contentful.

**Evidence 1** — `.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md` line 57, verbatim (confirmed):
> - CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level (DMU-035, partial resolution 2026-05-15): **SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful). Still Open: Sparro to define field schema before custom build.

**Evidence 2** — same file, line 81 (Open Items), which I found and you didn't cite:
> - CMS-editable on-page SEO field — field schema to be defined by Sparro (DMU-035, **location resolved as SFCC**)

This is the stronger quote. Line 57 says "partial resolution"; line 81 says the *location* specifically is **resolved**. What remains open is only the field schema, owed by Sparro.

**Evidence 3** — `.docs/prd/plp.md`, under `### 1.2 Editorial / SEO Content (SPR-03, SPR-04 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)`:
> - Configurable title, description, and hero image per category page **via Business Manager.**

⚠️ **Correction to your brief:** that's **line 19**, not line 18. Line 18 is the "read more" line. Substance holds, cite is off by one.

**Evidence 4** — Confluence 478248974 ("04.1.19 Data Migration / SEO / Analytics Requirements - Mapping"), the authoritative requirement→story map, verbatim:
> | DMU-036 | SEO | The system will provide a CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level. | SFCC-22 (SEO & Analytics & A/B Testing) | **SFCC-577 — PLP SEO Copy Content Field (CMS-Editable, BM-Configurable)** | No PLP override or Contentful wiring exists yet — net-new build. See comment on SFCC-577. |

**SFCC-748 does not appear anywhere in that mapping table.** The requirement is mapped to SFCC-577 alone.

⚠️ **New finding — DMU numbering has drifted between sources.** This requirement is **DMU-035** in the local PRD but **DMU-036** in Confluence (where DMU-036 locally is `robots.txt`). Identical requirement text, different IDs. Worse: **the Confluence version omits the "(not Contentful)" resolution entirely.** So whichever source someone reads determines whether they think this decision exists. That alone explains how 748 got written.

**Evidence 5** — Confluence 5.9.2 / 5.9 (Contentful content-model pages). The agreed model set is *"The 12 content models"* — Hero, Editorial Card, Simple Text, Rich Text, Accordion, Boutique, Table, Pull Quote, Media Collection, Look, Video, ShoppableProduct — plus 4 shipped global models (Footer Config, Header Navigation, Header Nav Item, UI Copy). **There is no SEO content type and no breadcrumb content type on that list.** Breadcrumb appears only as a component with no backing model:
> | Breadcrumb | Likely derived from the page's own position/hierarchy rather than authored content — to confirm. |

**The honest counterweight, which matters:** the team is already drifting toward Contentful *regardless of the PRD*, and nobody has recorded the change.
- **SFCC-749 is 5 points and already "Ready for Development"** with 13 ACs that assume Contentful throughout. Someone signed that off.
- **SFCC-95** (Squad-B, epic SFCC-22 — the *same* epic as the BM-titled SFCC-577) says verbatim: *"The section headings and body copy are **CMS-managed in Contentful** and are page-contextual."*
- Tim Lavelle's comment on SFCC-577 itself (2026-09-11) discusses **Contentful** modelling, not BM: *"The Rich Text/Simple Text Contentful primitives from the CMS migration work already exist though, which cuts down the content-modelling side of this."*

So Squad-B's own two tickets **contradict each other** — SFCC-577's title says BM-Configurable, SFCC-95's body says Contentful. This is not "748 is wrong and everyone else is right." It's **an unrecorded decision reversal that nobody has written down anywhere**, and the PRD is the only artefact still holding the original line. Per AGENTS.md's Doc-integrity rule this is a hard stop: cite the doc, ask whether the doc is stale or the ticket is wrong, don't proceed either way.
